548. Ala, to adorn, to be competent or able, to prevent. Pre. अलति । Perfect आल । In forming the Aorist, the following sutra applies:—

2330. The Vṛiddhi is substituted for the short a, when it is immediately followed by the final r or l of a root, before the Parasmaipada sich-Aorist.

"The 'ल्र्' in the sūtra is in the Genitive case, the case affix is elided here.

Note:—If the word 'anta' in the sūtra be taken to mean 'a member or a part,' and 'lranta' be taken as a Bahuvrīhi, meaning 'that which has a l or a r as its member'; and the word ataḥ be taken as separate, then there would be no necessity of using the word anta in the sūtra; the tadanta-vidhi would have been enough, and would have shown that l or r must be final. And in that view the rule would have applied to aśvalīt also. If the word anta be taken to mean 'proximity' as it is taken by the Kāśikā in the above note, then if the compound be genitive Tatpurusha, the rule would apply to ✓ Rap, ✓ Trap, ✓ Śalla &c: because here r or l is in proximity to the a of the root stem. But if the compound be Karmadhāraya, meaning 'the proximate l or r' then anta being attributive ought to have stood first in the compound. To avoid all these difficulties the author says 'lr in the genitive case &c.' The sūtra, therefore, means:—

If the l or r is in the proximity of a short a, then of a stem ending in such a l or r, there is the vṛiddhi of a, when the Parasmaipada s-aorist follows. This supersedes the prohibition of VII. 2. 4. S. 2268; and the option of VII. 2. 7. S. 2281. Thus the aorist will be agālīt | (अगालीत्) as in mā bhavān gālīt [where the augment a is elided, but the long ā is heard].

Some say the root Ala is svaritet. The root takes the ātmanepada affixes also, according to their view. Thus alate.

entries.english:
2332. The vikarana उ comes (instead of शप्) after the roots धिन्व 'to please', and कृण्व 'to hurt', when a sarvadhatuka affix denoting the agent follows; and in these verbs अ is the substitute of the final व of these two roots.

The roots धिन्व, and कृण्व, belong both to the Bhvadi class. Thus धिन्+व्+उ+ति = धिन्+अ+उ+ति = धिन् + उ + ति (The अ is elided by VI. 4. 48. S. 2308) = धिनोति 'he pleases.' It might be asked, why there is no guna of the short penultimate of धिन् by rule VII. 3. 86 which requires the base to be gunated before the sarvadhatuka affix उ? The answer is to be found in sutra I. 1. 57 the zero substitute of अ, though a blank is like the former occupant (sthanivat) and thus prevents guna and is not considered penultimate, while the उ itself is gunated before the पित् affixes, though it is not gunated before non-pit affixes, as धिनुतः, धिन्वन्ति । In forming the First Person dual and plural, the next sutra gives an option.

Note:—Though the root धिन्व Dhinv originally is not one that ends in अ, and it assumes the form धिन Dhina subsequently, yet at the time of applying the Ardhadhatuka affix उ, it is अ-ending, so the lopa rule VI. 4. 48 S. 2308 applies.
entries.note: Devanagari line has misprinted serial number २३३१ and corrupt Ashtadhyayi reference.

entries.english:
2333. The उ of the vikaranas, where not preceded by a conjunct consonant, may be elided optionally before a personal ending beginning with म or व.

Thus धिन्वः or धिनुवः, धिन्मः or धिनुमः । Before the affix मिप्, however, there will be guna, by the subsequent rule because the affix is पित् and thus we have धिनोमि ॥

In forming the Imperative the following rule applies:—

2334. The Imperative हि is elided after the उ of an affix, in the vikarana with which the Present-stem is made, provided that the उ is not preceded by a conjunct consonant.

The affix with which the Present-stem is made is उ and श्नु ॥ After this उ, the Imperative हि is elided.

Thus धिनु ॥

Note:—Why after 'उ'? Observe लुनीहि, पुनीहि । Why do we say "उ being part of the vikarana or affix"? Observe कुहि, रुहि, here उ is part of the root itself, and not of the vikarana. Why do we say 'not preceded by a conjunct consonant'? Observe आप्नुहि, राध्नुहि, तक्ष्णुहि ॥

Note:—The elision of हि after the उ of the vikarana is optional in the Vedas; as आतनुहि यातुधानान्, धिनुहि यज्ञपतिम्, तेन मा भागिनं कुरु ॥

The augment आट् being nitya (compulsory and never set aside by any rule) takes effect prior to the application of the rule requiring elision of उ. Thus व् and म् being preceded by आ, there is no occasion for applying VI. 4. 107 S. 2333; for उ is not followed by व or म but by आव or आम. Thus we have in the Dual and Plural धिनवाव and धिनवाम ॥

entries.english:
2335. There is elision of ढ when a ढ follows.
Though this sûtra is read in the division of Grammar which is governed by पदाधिकार, yet this elision takes place only when the ढ is not at the end of a pada. Thus गाढा from गाढ् + ता । The ह् is changed to ढ् by VIII. 2. 31 § 324, and the त् is first changed to ध् by VIII. 2. 40 § 2280 and then to ढ by VIII. 4. 41, § 113. Thus गाढ् + ढा । The first ढ is elided by this sûtra and we get गाढा । The change of ध into ढ by VIII. 4. 41, should be considered as valid and siddha for the purposes of this rule, otherwise this rule will find no scope.
Note:—The form जघाक्षे is thus evolved :— गाह् + थास् = गाह् + से (III. 4. 80. § 2236) = गाढ् + से (VIII. 2. 31. § 321) = घाढ् + से (VIII. 2. 37 § 336) = घाढ् + षे (VIII. 2. 41 § 295) = घाक्ष, and with reduplication अघाक्षे ।
680. Gahu, to stir up. Pre. गाहते । Per. जगाहे । जगाहिषे or जघाक्षे । जगाहिध्वे, ध्वे or जगाढ्वे । I Fut. गाहिता or गाढा । II Fut. गाहिष्यते or घाक्ष्यते । Imperative. गाहताम् । Imper. अगाहत । Poten. गाहेत । Bene. गाहिषीष्ट or घाक्षीष्ट । Aorist गाहिष्ट or अगाढ । अघाक्षाताम् । अघाक्षत । अगाढाः । अगाढ्वम् । अघाक्षि । Caus. गाहयति । Aorist अजीगहत् । Desi. जिघाक्षते or जिगाहिषते । Inten. जागाह्यते । Yan luk जागोढि । Ger. गाढ्वा or गाहित्वा ॥
गृहू ६८१ ग्रहणे । गर्हते । जगृहे ॥
*ऋदुपधेभ्यो लिटः कित्त्वं गुणात् पूर्वविप्रतिषेधेन* ॥
जगृहिषे-जगृक्षे । जगृढ्वे । गर्हिता-गर्ढा । गर्हिष्यते-घर्क्ष्यते । गर्हिषीष्ट-घृक्षीष्ट । लुङि । अगर्हिष्ट । इडभावे ॥
681. Grihu, 'to take,'
Thus Pre. गर्हते । Per. जगृहे । Before the augment इट् the following Vartika applies:
Vārt:—The affixes of लिट् (Perfect) are कित् in the case of roots that have a penultimate ऋ; and this कित्-condition takes effect before the application of Guna rule, by debarring the subsequent in anticipation. The sutra requiring Guna, namely, पुगन्तलघूपधस्य (VII. 3. 86 § 2189) being subsequent to the कित्त्व rule, would have applied first, but it is set aside by this vartika. Thus we have जगृहिषे or जगृक्षे । जगृढ्वे । &c. Aorist अगर्हिष्ट ।
But when it does not take the augment इट्, the following rule applies in forming its aorist.

entries.english:
2336. After a verb that ends in a consonant (श्, ष्, स् and ह्) and has an इक् vowel for its penultimate letter, and does not take इट् (VII. 2. 10), क्स is the substitute of च्लि.
Thus अधुक्षत् = दुह् + क्स + त् ।
Before the affixes beginning with a vowel, the अ of क्स is elided by the following sûtra.

2337. The अ (of the Aorist characteristic) क्स is elided before an affix beginning with a vowel.
The elision is of the final of Ksa, and not of the whole affix (See I. 1. 52. § 42). Thus अधुक्षाताम् । अधुक्षन्त ॥
Note:— Why do we say 'when ending in श्, ष्, स् and ह्' ? Observe ‹?›, ‹?›; here ‹?› is employed. Why do we say 'having an इक् for its penultimate इ, उ, ऋ or ऌ' ? Observe ‹?› । Why do we say 'not having an intermediate इट्' ? Observe ‹?› and ‹?› । See VII. 2. 4 and VIII. 2. 28.
Had the अ not been elided before आताम् and आथाम्, then इय् must have been substituted for it according to VII. 2. 81. Why do we say before an affix beginning with a vowel? Observe अधुक्षत्, अधुक्षताम् । Why do we say क्स and not only स? So that the elision should not take place here, as ‹?›, ‹?›, ‹?›, वत्साः, ‹?›, ‹?› ।
681. Grihu, to take. Pre. गर्हते । Per. जगृहे । जगृहिषे or जगृक्षे । जगृढ्वे । ‹?› । I Fut. गर्हिता, गर्ढा । II Fut. गर्हिष्यते, घर्क्ष्यते । Imperative गर्हताम् । Imper. ‹?› । Poten. गर्हेत । Bene. गर्हिषीष्ट or घृक्षीष्ट । Aorist अगर्हिष्ट or अधुक्षत । अगर्हिषाताम् or अधुक्षाताम् । अगर्हिषत । अगर्हिष्ठाः or अधुक्षथाः । अगर्हिढ्वम् or ‹?› । अगर्हिषि or अधुक्षि । अगर्हिष्वहि or अधुक्ष्वहि । Desi. जिगर्हिषते, जिघृक्षते । Inten. ‹?› । Yan luk ‹?› । Noun ‹?› । Ger. गर्हित्वा । ‹?› ।
681. A. Glaha cha, to take. Swami, Kasyapa and Simmata read glaha. Pre. ग्लहते । Noun, ग्लहः ॥
682. Ghushi, to be beautiful or brilliant. Some read it as Ghas. Chandra and Kasyapa read it as घुषि with a penultimate उ. Pre. घोषते । Per. जुघुषे । I Fut. घोशिता । Desi. जुघुषिषते । Inten. जोघुष्यते । Yan luk. जोघोष्टि । लङ् 2nd P. अजोघुट् । लङ् अजोघुन् ।
Here end the roots whose final is a sibilant and which are Atmanepadi.
Herewith commence roots ending with a sibilant and which are Parasmaipadi.

entries.english:
683. Ghuṣir, not to proclaim. 2. To sound. The word aviśabdana means non-viśabdana. The word viśabdana means 'promise'. According to others the word is śabda only and the root means 'to sound'. The indicatory ir makes the rule III. 1. 57, S. 2269 applicable in the aorist. When the root has all other meanings except that of 'proclaiming' (viśabdana) it is read here. When it has the meaning of viśabdana (proclaiming), it belongs to Churâdi class (187). Pre. घोषति । Per. जुघोष । Fut. घोषिता । Aorist अघुषत् or अघोषीत् । ‹?› । Caus. घोषयति । Aorist अजूघुषत् । Desi. जुघुविषति, or जुघोषिषति । Inten. जोघुष्यते । Yañ luk जोघोष्टी । लङ् 2nd S. अजोघोः । लङ् 3rd S. अजोघोः । Past Part. Pass. घुष्टः (VII. 2. 23, S. 3063). Ger. घुषित्वा or घोषयित्वा । Noun घुष्टा ॥
684. व्याप्तौ 'to pervade.' As अक्षति । But by the following sutra, it takes the vikaraṇa श्नु also.
entries.note: Continuation from preceding page without sutra heading; SK 2337 inferred from sequence before 2338.

entries.english:
2338. The vikaraṇa श्नु is optionally employed after the root अक्षू 'to pervade,' when a sârvadhâtuka affix denoting an agent, follows.
Thus अक्ष्णोति or अक्षति 'he pervades or obtains.' D. अक्ष्णुतः Pl. अक्ष्णुवन्ति ।
684. Akshû, to pervade. Because the root has an indicatory long ū, the iṭ augment is optional. Pre. अक्षति, अक्षतः, अक्षन्ति । Per. आनक्ष or आनक्षिव । आनक्षिथ or आनष्ठ । I Fut. अक्षिता, or अक्ष्टा । II Fut. अक्षिष्यति or अक्ष्यति (= अक्ष् + स्यति = अक् + ष् + स्यति VIII. 2. 41, S. 295 = अक् + स्यति; the ष् is elided by VIII. 2. 29, S. 380 = अक्ष्यति) । Imperative अक्षतु or अक्ष्णोतु । अक्ष्णुहि । अक्ष्णवानि &c. Imperf. आक्षत्, आक्ष्णोत् । 1. S. आक्ष्णवम् । Pote. अक्षेत् or अक्ष्णुयात् । Bene. अक्ष्यात् । Aorist आक्षीत्, (आक्षत्, without augment by VII. 2. 4, S. 2368) D. आक्षिष्टाम् । P. आक्षिषुः । When अङ् is not added we have — आक्षीत् । आष्टाम् । आक्षुः । Caus. अक्षयति । Aorist आचिक्षत् । Desi. अचिक्षिषति or अचिक्षति । Past Part. Pass. अक्ष्टः । Ger. अक्षित्वा or अक्ष्ट्वा । Noun अक्षः 'eye.'
तक्ष ६८५, त्वक्ष ६८६ तनूकरणे ।
685. तनूकरणे 'to make thin.' As तक्षति । This root also takes श्नु optionally by the following sutra.

2339. The affix श्नु is optionally employed after the root तक्ष 'to make thin' when a sârvadhâtuka affix denoting an agent, follows.
Thus तक्षति or तक्ष्णोति काष्ठम् 'he planes the wood.' Why do we say when meaning to make thin? Observe, वाग्भिः संतक्षति । 'he cuts with speech.'

Pre. लसति । Nouns आलस्यम् । अलसः । लसः । विलासिन् (III. 2. 143). घस्लृ ७४७ अदने । अयं न सार्वत्रिकः । ‹लुटाद्यन्यतरस्याम्› (२४२४) इत्यादेर्घस्लादेशविधानात् । ततश्च यत्र लिङ्गं वचनं वास्ति तत्रैवास्य प्रयोगः । अत्रैव पाठः शपि परस्मैपदे लिङ्गम् । लृदित्करणमङ् । अनिट्कारिकासु पाठो बलादार्धधातुके । क्वमरचि तु विशिष्योपादानम् । घसति । घस्ता ॥ 747. Ghaslri, to eat. This root is defective and is not conjugated in all tenses and moods. Because it is ordained as the substitute of अद् in the Perfect (see II. 4. 40). Had it been an independent root, perfect in all its conjugation, there would have been no necessity of that sutra. Therefore this root घस् is used in those tenses and moods only where it is either specifically ordained or where its presence may be deduced. Its being read in the Bhvadi class shows that it is conjugated as a Bhvadi root, and not as an Adadi root though a substitute of अद् । Moreover it is Parasmaipadi. The indicatory लृ shows that the Aorist is formed with अङ् । This root is read in the list of the Anit roots (see p. 73): in order that no इट् augment is to be added in Ardhadhatuka affixes beginning with a वल् consonant. Thus by III. 2. 160 it takes the affix क्वमरच् ; but no augment is added before this affix. As घस्मरः । Pre. घसति । Per. जघास । I Fut. घस्ता । In forming the 2nd Future the following sutra 2342 applies:— II Fut. घत्स्यति (VII. 4. 49). Imperative घसतु । Imper. अघसत् । Poten. घसेत् । The root is not found in the Benedictive. The Aorist is formed by the following sutra 2343. Aorist अघसत् । Nouns घस्मरः । घासः । घातिः ॥

entries.english: 2342. त is substituted for the final स of a root before an Ardhadhatuka affix beginning with स ॥ As घस् + स्यति = घत् + स्यति = घत्स्यति । Why do we say 'when ending in स'? Observe वक्ष्यति । Why do we say 'beginning with स'? Observe घासः, वासः ॥ Why an Ardhadhatuka? Observe आस्से, वस्से, from आस, 'to sit' and वस्, 'to cover'; both Adadi roots.

entries.english: 2343. अङ् is the substitute of च्लि, after the verbs पुष 'to nourish' and the rest, द्युत् 'to shine', and the rest, and the verbs having an indicatory ऌ, when the affixes of the Parasmaipada follow. Thus अघसत् । The verbs classed as पुषादि, are a subdivision of the 4th conjugational verbs; and द्युतादि verbs belong to the 1st conjugation. As पुष, अपुषत् 'he nourished'; द्युत, अद्युतत् 'he shone'; गम्लृ, अगमत् 'he went.' But not so in the Atmanepada; as व्यद्योतिष्ट, अद्योतिष्ट. जर्ज ७४८, चर्च ७४९, झर्झ ७५० परिभाषणहिंसातर्जनेषु । 748. Jarja, 749. Charcha, 750. Jharjha, to say, 2. to injure, 3. to threaten. The roots जर्ज and झर्झ belong to the Tudadi class also, and give rise to the same forms. The difference is in the accent only. 'चर्च to study' is Churadi. Pre. जर्जति ॥ 749. Charcha, Pre. चर्चति ॥ 750. Jharjha, Pre. झर्झति । Noun झर्झरः ॥ पिसृ ७५१, पेसृ ७५२, विसृ ७५३, वेसृ ७५४, पिशृ ७५५, पेशृ ७५६ गतौ । पिपिसितुः । विषेसतुः ॥ 751. Pisri, 752. Pesri, to go, to move. The root पिस would become पेस by guna; the reading two roots separately is for the sake of कित् affixes, such as those of Perfect. Pre. पेसति । Per. पिपेस । पिपिसतुः । Caus. पेसयति, Aor. अपीपिसत् । Inten. पेपिष्यते । Nouns:— पेस्वरः । (III. 2. 175). 752. Pesri, Pre. पेसति । Per. पिपेस । पिपेसतुः । Inten. पेपेस्यते ॥ 753. Visri, to go. Pre. वेसति । Per. विवेस । विविसतुः । Inten. वेविश्यते ॥ 754. Vesri, to go. Pre. वेसति । Per. विवेस । विविसतुः ॥ 755. Pisri, to go, to move. Pre. पेशति । Per. पिपेश । पिपिशतुः । Inten. पेपिश्यते ॥ 756. Pesri, to go. Pre. पेशति । Per. विपेश । पिपेशतुः । Inten. पेपेश्यते ॥ हसे ७५७ हसने । दित्त्वाच्च न वृद्धिः । अहसीत् ॥ 757. Hase, to laugh. Pre. हसति । Per. जहास । I Fut. हसिता । Aorist. अहसीत् । (There is no Vriddhi, as the root has got an indicatory इ । VII. 2. 5.) entries.english:
2344. There is vocalisation of the half-vowel of the reduplicate of द्युत, and स्वापि (Causative of स्वप्) ॥

As दिद्युते । विदिद्योतिषते विदिद्युतिषते, (I. 2. 26) विदेद्युत्यते ॥

In forming the aorist the following sûtra applies.

2345. After the verbs dyut 'to shine,' and the rest the terminations of the Parasmaipada are optionally employed, when the affixes of lun (aorist) follow.

The Dyutâdi verbs are 22 in number (Bhuâdi 777 and twenty one that follow it up to घट 'to try.' By the use of the word द्युद्भ्यः in the plural in the sûtra, the force is that of "and the rest". These verbs are anudâtteta and so by sûtra, I. 3. 12 they would have been invariably âtmanepadî, this aphorism makes them optionally so.

777. √ Dyuta, to shine. The roots beginning with dyut and ending with Kripâ are udâtta and anudâttet. Pre. द्योतते । In forming the Perfect there is vocalisation by VII. 4. 67 § 2344. Per. दिद्युते । विदिद्युताते । I Fut. द्योतिता । II Fut. द्योतिष्यते । Impera. द्योतताम् । Imper. अद्योतत । Pote. द्योतेत । Bene. द्योतिषीष्ट । Aorist अद्युतत् or अद्योतिष्ट । The root is optionally Parasmaipadî by I. 3. 91. § 2345. When Parasmaipadî the Aorist is formed by अङ् because it belongs to पुषादि class. See explanation. Per. मिमिदे । I Fut. मेदिता । Aorist. अमेदिष्ट or अमिदत् । Past Part. Pass. मिन्नः । Nouns मेदुरः । मिदः ॥

2346. For i in mid there is substituted a guna before such a sit affix, where the indicatory s stands in the beginning of the affix.

Note:— As मेदति, मेद्यतः, मेद्यन्ति ॥ Why mid only? Observe स्विद्यति, स्विद्यन्ति । The root ञिमिदा belongs both to the Bhvâdi and the Divâdi classes. The Bhvâdi mid will get guna before sap by virtue of VII. 3. 86, but the Divâdi mid would not have got guna before syan, as this affix is nit (I. 2. 4): hence the necessity of this sûtra. Before non sit affixes there is no guna, as मिमिदे, मेमिद्यते ॥

The phrase शिति 'where the affix has an indicatory s' is understood here from the preceding Ashtadhyayi sûtra VII. 3. 75. The word sit should be explained as a Karmadharaya compound meaning s indicatory (शश्चासौ इच्च = शित्). Then siti would mean by tadâdividhi mântena and the affix that begins with an indicatory s. Therefore the affix es (III. 4. 81) though a sit affix, does not begin with an indicatory s, and hence before this affix there will be no guna. Hence we have मिमिदे in the Perfect.

entries.english:
2347. After the verbs 'vrit' to exist &c., Parasmaipada is optionally employed when the affixes sya (second Future and conditional) and san (Desiderative) follow.

The वृतादि verbs are five in number and are included in the द्युतादि subclass. They are वृत् 'to be,' वृध् 'to grow', शृध् 'to fart or break wind', स्यन्दू 'to ooze', and कृपू 'to be able.' As Future वर्त्स्यति, 'it will be,' Conditional अवर्त्स्यत् ; Desiderative विवृत्सति &c.

In other tenses than the above, they are always Atmanepadi. As वर्तते ॥

entries.english:
2348. The Parasmaipada Ardhadhatuka affixes beginning with s do not get the augment it after vrit and the three roots that follow it.

Thus वृत् — वर्त्स्यति, अवर्त्स्यत्, विवृत्सति । स्यन्दू — स्यन्त्स्यति, अस्यन्त्स्यत्, सिस्यन्त्सति । कृपू — कल्प्स्यति, अकल्प्स्यत्, चिक्लृप्सति । वृध् — वर्त्स्यति, अवर्त्स्यत्, विवृत्सति ।

The वृतादि roots are four: वृत्, वृध्, शृध्, and स्यन्दू (Bhu. 795-798). In the examples, the Parasmaipada forms are shown, because these roots are optionally Parasmaipadi by I. 3. 92 before स्य and सन् ।

Obj:—The word चतुर्भ्यः may conveniently have been omitted from the sutra. A reference to the Dhatupatha will show that the वृतादि roots form a subdivision of द्युतादि roots, and stand at the end of Dyutadi class. So that the sutra न वृद्भ्यः would have been enough, and there would have been no uncertainty or vagueness about it, for the word वृतादि would mean 'the roots वृत् &c. with which the Dyutadi class ends. Thus we shall get the five roots 795 वृत्, 796 वृध्, 797 शृधु शब्दकुत्सायाम् ; 798 स्यन्दू प्रस्रवणे and कृपू सामर्थ्ये । As regards the last root कृप्, we shall find from the next sutra, that the present sutra applies to this root also. Or we can change the order of the roots, putting कृपू first, and वृत् &c. after it, so that वृतादि will mean four roots only. Whether vritadi be taken to mean the five or the four roots, the word चतुर्भ्यः is redundant.

The word चतुर्भ्यः is used in order that the prohibition contained in this sutra may debar the option which the root स्यन्दू would have taken, because of its indicatory long ऌ (VII. 2. 44). For this 'option' is an antaranga operation, because it applies to all ardhadhatuka affixes; while the 'prohibition' of the present sutra is a bahiranga, because it applies to those affixes only which begin with स । So that the 'prohibition' of this sutra would not have debarred the 'option' of VII. 2. 44: and in the Parasmaipada स्यन्दू would have had two forms; which, however, is not the case because of the word चतुर्भ्यः by which the 'prohibition' is extended to स्यन्दू also. Thus in the Parasmaipada, we have only one form, as, स्यन्त्स्यति ; but in the Atmanepada we have two forms स्यन्दिष्यते or स्यन्त्स्यते ॥

The word 'Parasmaipada' is understood in this sutra, so that the prohibition does not apply to Atmanepada affixes: as वर्तिषीष्ट, वर्तिष्यते, अवर्तिष्यत, विवर्तिष्यते, स्यन्दिषीष्ट or स्यन्त्सीष्ट । Moreover, with regard to Atmanepada also, the इट् is added to these roots when they stand in the same 'pada' with the affixes. But when the Atmanepada affixes are added not to the roots 'vrit' &c., but to the roots which are derived from the nominal bases formed from vrit &c., then the root is not in the same pada with the affix, and the prohibition of this sutra will apply. As विवृत्सित्रीयते । Moreover, the rule applies, as we have said to the affixes 'standing in the same 'pada' with the 'roots'; therefore it will apply to Desiderative roots, as विवृत्सति, though शप् here intervenes between the ardhadhatuka affix सन् and the Parasmaipada तिप्; so also, an ekadesa though sthanivat and therefore an intervention, will not be considered so for the purposes of this rule, as विवृत्सयति ; so also in विवृत्सयते । The prohibition, moreover, applies to ‹?› affixes, and where there is luk-elision of Parasmaipada affixes. As विवृत्सितौ and विवृत्सिताः where the Imperative सिप् is luk-elided, and being so elided, the force of Parasmaipada does not here remain by न लुमताङ्गस्य (I. 1. 63); hence the above isht.

वृधु ७९६ वृद्धौ ।

स्यन्दू ७९८ प्रस्रवणे । स्यन्दते । सस्यन्दे । सस्यन्दिषे-सस्यन्त्से । सस्यन्दिध्वे-सस्यन्द्ध्वे । सस्यन्दिवहे-सस्यन्स्वहे । स्यन्दिता-स्यन्ता । 'वृद्भ्यः स्यसनोः' (२३४७) इति परस्मैपदे कृते ऌत इद्विकल्पमन्तरङ्गमपि बाधित्वा चतुर्ग्रहणसामर्थ्यात् 'न वृद्भ्यः' (२३४८) इति निषेधः । स्यन्त्स्यति स्यन्दिष्यते स्यन्त्स्यते । स्यन्दिषीष्ट-स्यन्त्सीष्ट । 'द्युद्भ्यो लुङि' (२३४६) इति परस्मैपदपक्षे ङि । नलोपः । अस्यदत्-अस्यन्त्स्यत् । आस्यन्त्साताम् । आस्यन्त्सन् । अस्यन्त्स्यत्-अस्यन्दिष्यत्-अस्यन्त्स्यत ॥

Pre. स्यन्दते । Per. सस्यन्दे । सस्यन्दिषे or सस्यन्त्से । सस्यन्दिध्वे or सस्यन्द्ध्वे । सस्यन्दिवहे or सस्यन्स्वहे । I Fut. स्यन्दिता or स्यन्ता । II Fut. स्यन्दिष्यते or स्यन्त्स्यति or स्यन्त्स्यते । Impera. स्यन्दताम् ।

Condi. (1) अस्यन्दिष्यत or (2) अस्यन्त्स्यत or (3) अस्यत्स्यत् । Desi. सिस्यन्दिषते, सिस्यन्त्सते, सिस्यन्त्सति । Inten. सेष्यन्द्यते । Past Part. स्यन्नः । Ger. स्यन्दित्वा or स्यन्त्वा । Nouns सिन्धुः । सैन्धवः ॥

2349. ष is optionally the substitute of the स of स्यन्द, after the prepositions अनु, वि, परि, अभि and नि, when the subject is not a living being.

The root स्यन्दू प्रस्रवणे is anudatta. Thus अनुष्यन्दते । विष्यन्दते । परिष्यन्दते । अभिष्यन्दते तैलम् । निष्यन्दते । अनुस्यन्दते । विस्यन्दते । परिस्पन्दते । Thus अनुष्यन्दते or अनुस्यन्दते जलम् ॥

Why do we say 'when the subject is not a living being'? Observe अनुस्यन्दते हस्ती । The option of this sûtra will apply, when the subject is a compound of living and non-living beings. Thus अनुस्यन्देते or अनुष्यन्देते मत्स्योदके । The subject here is a Dvandva compound, and it is not in the singular number because of II. 4. 6. The word अप्राणिषु is a Paryudâsa and not a Prasajya-Pratishedha. If it be the latter sort of prohibition, then the force will be on the word living, and in a compound like मत्स्योदके, consisting of living and non-living beings, the prohibition will apply because it has a living being in it, and so the ष will be no षत्व । In the other view, the force is on the word non-living, and because the compound contains a non-living being, therefore the option will be applied, and the presence of the living being along with it will be ignored.

The anuvritti of परि, वि and नि is understood here from VIII. 3. 70. So these words could well have been omitted from the sutra, which might have then been अन्वभिभ्यां च स्यन्दतेरप्राणिषु and by the force of च we would draw in the anuvritti of परि &c.

799 कॢपू सामर्थ्ये । In conjugating this root, the following applies :

2350. For the र of the root कॢप् there is substituted ल ।

The word कृपा is compounded of कॢप् + ङस् । The term कॢपि is used with the force of the genitive, the case-ending is considered as latent. It is repeated. The meaning is "In the place of the र of कॢप् there is ल । In the place of the र-sound which is a portion of the ऋ of कॢप् and therefore which may be considered as like-र there is substituted something which is like ल । That is when कॢप् assumes by guna the form कल्प, then for र is substituted ल and we have कल्प । But even with ऋ, a l-sound like ऌ is substituted for ऋ, and we have कॢप्." So also in other cases of like nature.

The र here merely indicates the sound, and includes both the single consonant and the same consonant of the vowel ऋ । So also with ल । So that for the single र there is substituted ल ; and for र when a portion of ऋ, the ऌ is substituted, i.e. ऋ becomes ऌ । Thus कल्प + ता = कल्प्ता, as in the sûtra लुटि च कॢपः (I. 3. 93), कल्प्ता, कल्प्तारौ, कल्प्तारः । कॢप्तः । कॢप्तवान् ॥

The word कॢपि is derived from the root कृपू by vocalisation, as it has been enumerated in Bhidadi class (कृपेः संप्रसारणं III. 3. 104). The vocalised root-form is not to be taken here, as it is a lakshanika form.

Vart :— The words कृपण, कृपाण, कृपीट, कर्पूर &c. are also from कृप् । Or by the Unâdi diversity, the change does not take place.

Vart :— Optionally so of वाल &c. As, बालः or वारः, शूलम् or शूरम्, असुरः or असुलः, अलम् or अरम्, अङ्गुलिः or अङ्गुरिः ॥

Vart :— Optionally so in the Vedas, or when names, of कपिलका &c. As वाशिरक or वाशिलकः, तिस्पिलोकम् or तिपिटकम्, लोमानि or रोमानि, पांशुरं or पांशुलं, कर्मा or कल्मा, शुकः or शुकः, कम्मर्व, कम्मर्य ॥

Some say 'र and ल are one': and operations regarding र may be performed with regard to ल ॥

In forming the First Future, the next sûtra applies.

2351. After the verb kḷp 'to be fit', Parasmaipada is optionally employed, when luṭ (1st Future) is affixed, as well as when sya and san are affixed.

The verb कॢप् is one of the five verbs of the sub-class, वृतादि । (I. 3. 92. S. 2347). Therefore it will take both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada, when the affixes स्य or सन् follow. The present sûtra makes the additional declaration in the case of the 1st Future or लुट् । Thus in Luṭ we have :— कल्प्तासि or कल्पितासे ; in the 2nd Future we have :— कल्पिष्यति or कल्पिष्यते ; in the Desiderative we have :— चिकल्पिषति or चिकल्पिषते ; in the Conditional we have :— अकल्पिष्यत् or अकल्पिष्यत ॥

entries.english:
2352. The (Parasmaipada) Ardhadhatuka affixes beginning with s, and the affix तास् (the sign of the Periphrastic Future) do not get the augment इट् after the root कॢप् except in the Atmanepada affixes.

Thus कल्प्ता, कल्प्स्यति, अचिक्लिप्सत्, चिक्लिप्सति । But कल्पितासे, कल्पिष्यते, अकल्पिष्यत, चिकल्पिषते in the Atmanepada.

In the case of कॢप् also, the इट् is added to the ardhadhatuka affixes in the Atmanepada, when the root stands in the same pada with the affixes and there is prohibition everywhere else. So also there is prohibition before krit-affixes, and the luk-elision of Parasmaipada. As चिक्लिप्सिता, चिक्लिप्सुः त्वम् ॥

According to Padamanjari, these two sutras could have been shortened thus :— (1) न वृद्भ्यः पञ्चभ्यः, (2) तासि च ; and "कृपः" could well have been omitted. The तास् comes only after कॢप् and not after other roots of Vritadi class, in Parasmaipada [I. 3. 92 and 93]. Therefore, there is no fear that the prohibition तासि च will apply to the other roots of vritadi, but only to 'kḷp,' because the word परस्मैपदेषु is understood here ; and as no roots of vritadi class take Parasmaipada in the Periphrastic Future except 'kḷp', there is no fear of any ambiguity.

800 Ghaṭa, to be busy with, strive after. The Ghaṭadi roots are मित्, a designation which will be explained further on. The result of their being मित्, is that the root is shortened in the causative by VI. 4. 92 S. 2568 ; and there is optional lengthening before the affixes चिण् and णमुल् by VI. 4. 93 S. 2762. As घटयति, विघटयति । If so, how do you explain the lengthening in उद्घाटन and प्रविघाटयिता in "कमलवनोद्घाटनं कुर्वते ये" । and "प्रविघाटयिता समुत्पतन्हरिदश्वः कमलाकरानिव" इत्यादि । शृणु । घट संघाते belonging to the Churadi class. (No. 183). The above forms are from that root. It should not be said that that root is only a particular case of the present root, the sense of संघात being a species under the genus चेष्टा, and therefore that root is also mitadi. This we say because there is a specific prohibition "no other roots of the Churadi which take णि are मित् ।" The meaning of अहेतौ is that except the five roots घट् &c. no Churadi root which takes णिच् without change of sense is a मित् । For the हेतु or स्वार्थ णि is added only to Churadi roots. Pre. घटते । Per. जग़टे । I Fut. घटिता । II Fut. घटि-

816. √Vaṭa. 817. √Bhaṭa, to speak, converse. These two roots have already been taught before in वट वेष्टने No. 322, and भट भृतौ No. 329. They are repeated here, in order to give them the additional meaning of paribhâshaṇa, and make them मित् । Caus. वटयति । भटयति । No lengthening. Aor. अवाटि or अवटि । अभाटि or अभटि ॥

नट ८१८ नृतौ । नट्यमेव पूर्वमपि पठितं तत्रायं भेदः पूर्वं पठितस्य नाट्यमर्थः । यत्कारिषु नटव्यपदेशः । वाक्यार्थाभिनयो नाट्यम् । घटादौ तु नृत्तं नृत्यं चार्थः । यत्कारिषु नर्तकव्यपदेशः । पदार्थाभिनयो नृत्यम् । गात्रविक्षेपमात्रं नृत्तम् । केचित्पु घटादौ नद गतौ इति पठन्ति । गद गतौ इत्यन्ये । पर्युदासवाक्ये भाष्यकृता नाटि इति दीर्घपाठाल्लुटादित्वोपदेश एव ॥
818. √Naṭa, to dance. This root has also been taught before. See No. 332. The difference is this, the root taught before means nâṭyam or dramatic representation; and a person who does that is called naṭa 'an actor.' The representation on the stage by spoken words to express the sense of something is nâṭyam or drama. But the root given here means to dance, the appropriate verbal nouns being nṛityam or nṛittam, and not nâṭyam. The person who does this is called नर्तकः 'a dancer', and not नटः 'an actor'. The difference between nṛityam and nṛittam is this. Representing of an action or object such as by pantomime or gesticulation is nṛityam; while nṛittam is dancing pure and simple, mere movement of the body.

entries.sutra_ocr: २३५३ । व्यथो लिटि । ४ । ६८ ॥ व्यथोऽभ्यासस्य संप्रसारणं स्याल्लिटि । हलादिः शेषापवादः । यस्य हलादिः शेषेण निवृत्तिः । विव्यथे ॥

entries.english:
Some read नट नृत्तौ 'to bend, to bow'; in the Ghatadi list, and say the ghatadi nata means to bow. They give the illustration नाटयति शाखां 'He causes the branch to bend'. Others say that it means to go.
The ghatadi nata (i.e. the present root) is to be understood to have been enunciated with an initial षा, that is it is षाट नृत्तौ । The reason for this is that in the exceptions to the roots that are taught with an initial षा, the author of the Mahabhashya gives नाटि, i.e. the nata with long आ । The मित् root can never have long आ in the causative. See VI. 1. 65. already gone before. In other words, the present root नट and the root no. 322 are both षोपदेश and the Churadi root नाट is not so and is the root mentioned in sutra VI. 1. 65.
Note:—The representation of a scene may be by words (vakyartha abhinaya) and then it is drama or natyam. Or it may be by gesticulation without words (padartha abhinaya), and then it is called nrityam. Or there may be no representation at all, but mere rhythmic movements of limbs according to rules and then it is called nritta. Their respective nouns are nata 'an actor,' and narttaka 'a pantomime' or 'a dancer.'
The Causative of the Ghatadi नट is नाटयति 'he causes to dance'. The aorist is अनटीत् or अनाटीत् ॥

819. Shataka to resist, repel, push back, strike against. Pre. स्तकति । Per. तस्ताक । I Fut. स्तकिता । Caus. स्तकयति, स्तकयते । Aor. अतिष्टकत् । Pass. Aor. अस्तकि or अस्ताकि । Desi. तिस्तकिषति । Inten. तास्तक्यते । Yan luk तास्तक्ति ॥

820. Chaka to be satisfied, satiated. This root has already been taught as an Atmanepadi under No. 93. 'to be satisfied', and 'to resist.' It is Atmanepadi there. It is repeated here in order to make it a मित् root, and then to confine its meaning to satisfaction only. It is moreover Parasmaipadi now, because of its repetition in this list. Pre. चकति । Per. चचाक । I Fut. चकिता । Aorist अचाकीत् or अचकीत् । Caus. चकयति, चकयते । Aor. अचीचकत् । Pass. Aor. अचकि or अचाकि ॥
entries.sutra_ocr: चक ८२० तृप्तौ । तृप्तिप्रतिघातयोः पूर्वं पठितस्य तृप्तिमात्रे मित्त्वार्थोऽनुवादः । आत्मनेपदिषु पठितस्य परस्मैपदिष्वनुवादात्परस्मैपदम् ॥

entries.english: 821. Kakha to laugh. As it has an indicatory ए, there is no Vriddhi in the aorist. As अकखीत् । Pre. कखति । Per. चकाख । चकखतुः । I Fut. कखिता । Aorist अकखीत् । Caus. कखयति, कखयते । Pass. Aor. अकखि or अकाखि । Desi. चिकखिषति । Inten. चाकख्यते । Yan luk चाकक्ति ॥

entries.english: 822. Rage to doubt. Pre. रगति । Per. रराग ॥
823. Lage to adhere or stick to. Pre. लगति । Noun लग्नः ॥

824. Hrage. 825 Hlage, 826 Shage, 827 Shthage to hide, cover. Some read स्थगे instead of ष्टगे । But it is incorrect. Pre. हगति । Per. जह्राग । Aorist अह्रगीत् । Caus. ह्रगयति, ह्रगयते । Aor. अजिह्रगत् । Pass. Aor. अह्रागि or अह्रगि । Desi. जिह्रगिषति । Inten. जाह्रग्यते । Yan luk जाह्रक्ति ॥
825. Hlage. Pre. ह्लगति । Per. जह्लाग । I Fut. ह्लागिता । Aorist अह्लागीत् ॥
826. Shage. Pre. सगति । Per. ससाग । सेगतुः । सेगुः । Aorist असगीत् । Caus. सागयति, सगयते । Aor. असीसगत । Pass. Aor. असागि or असगि । Desi. सिसगिषति । Inten. सासग्यते । Yan luk सासक्ति ॥

827. Shthage. Pre. स्थगति । Per. तस्थाग । I Fut. स्थगिता । Aorist अस्थगीत् । Caus. स्थगयति, स्थगयते । Aor. असिस्थगत् । Pass. Aor. अस्थगि or अस्थागि । Desi. तिष्ठगिषति । Inten. तास्थग्यते । Yan luk तास्थक्ति ॥

828. Kage to act, perform. The word no chyate means "nothing is said". That is we do not give any specific meaning to the root Kage, because it denotes action in general. Some say it has many meanings and therefore no particular meaning is assigned. Pre. कगति । Per. चकाग । I Fut. कगिता । Aorist अकगीत् । Desi. चिकगिषति ॥
entries.sutra_ocr: कगे ८२८ नोच्यते । अस्यायमर्थ इति विशिष्य नोच्यते । क्रिया सामान्यार्थत्वात् । अनेकार्थत्वादित्यन्ये ॥

entries.english: 829. Aka, 830 Aga. To go or move tortuously like a serpent. Pre. अकति । Per. आक । I Fut. अकिता । Aorist आकीत् । मा भवानकीत् । Caus. आकयति । Aor. मा भवान् अचीकत । Pass. Aor. मा भवान् आकि or अकि । Desi. अचिकिषति ॥
830. Aga. Pre. अगति । Per. आग । I Fut. अगिता । Aorist आगीत् । Caus. आगयति, अगयते । Desi. अजिगिषति ॥

831. Kana, 832 Rana to go, to move. These two roots have the meaning 'to make noise' also. See Nos. 476 and 472. When they have that sense their causative is काणयति and राणयति । Pre. कणति । Per. चकाण । I Fut. काणिता । Caus. काणयति, कणयते । Pass. Aor. अकाणि or अकणि । Desi. चिकणिषति ॥
832. Rana, to go. Pre. रणति । Per. रराण । I Fut. रणिता । Caus. राणयति, रणयते ॥

833. Chana, 834 Sana, 835 Srana. To go as well as to give. According to some Sana means to go. Pre. चणति । Per. चचाण । चेणतुः । चेणुः । I Fut. चणिता । Aorist अचाणीत् ॥ अचणीत् । Caus. चाणयति, चणयते । Aor. अचीचणत् । Pass. Aor. अचाणि or अचणि । Desi. चिचणिषति । Inten. चञ्चण्यते । Yan luk चञ्चणीति ॥
entries.sutra_ocr: चण ८३३, शण ८३४, श्रण ८३५ दाने च । शण गतौ इत्यन्ये ॥

entries.english: 834. Sana. Pre. शणति । Per. शशाण । I Fut. शणिता । Aorist अशाणीत् । अशणीत् ॥
835. Srana. Pre. श्रणति । Per. शश्राण । I Fut. श्रणिता । Aorist अशश्राणीत् । अश्रणीत् ॥

836. Sratha (Santha), 837 Slatha (Klatha) 838 Kratha, 839 Klatha. To injure. Though the root क्रथ is a मित् root, yet it takes vriddhi in the Causative, because it has been particularised so in the sutra II. 3. 56. S. 610. As क्रथयति । The मित् operation takes place on this root in the चिण् and णमुल् affixes by VI. 4. 93 S. 2762, because that is a sutra subsequent to the nipatana sutra II. 3. 56. This मित् causes the lengthening before चिण् and णमुल् । As अक्रथि or अक्राथि । क्रथंक्रथम् or क्राथंक्राथम् । Pre. श्रन्थति । Per. शश्रन्थ । I Fut. श्रन्थिथा । Caus. श्रन्थयति, श्रन्थयते । Aor. अशिश्रन्थत् । Pass. aor. अश्रन्थि or अश्रान्थि । Desi. शिश्रन्थिषति । Inten. शाश्रन्ध्यते । Yan luk शाश्रन्थीति ॥
entries.sutra_ocr: श्रन्थ (शन्थ) ८३६, (ग्रन्थ) श्लथ ८३७, क्रथ ८३८, क्लथ ८३९ हिंसाार्थाः । जासिनिग्रहण- (६१०) इति सूत्रे क्राथेति मित्रोऽपि बुद्धिर्निपात्यते । कासयति । मित्वं तु निपातनात्परत्वात् चित्यमुलोः- (२७६२) इति दीर्घे चरितार्थम् । चक्रधि- चक्राधि । क्रथं कथम् । क्राथं क्राधम् ॥

entries.english: 837. Slatha. Pre. श्लथति । Per. शश्लाथ । I Fut. श्लथिता । Desi. शिश्लथिषति । Inten. शाश्लथ्यते ॥
838. Knatha, to injure. Pre. क्रथति । Per. चक्राथ । I Fut. क्रथिता ॥
839. Klatha. Pre. क्लथति । Per. चक्लाथ । I Fut. क्लथिता ॥

840. Vana (chana) to injure. By the force of the word च, the meaning of 'to injure' is drawn into it from the last. Some read it as Chana. Pre. वनति । Per. ववान । I Fut. वनिता । Caus. वनयति, वनयते । Pass. Aor. अवनि or अवानि ॥

841. Vanu. And Vanu also is not mentioned. That is to say that this Vanu is an original root and not a repetition of the Tanadi root Vanu to beg (VIII. 8). This we say because this Vanu has an indicatory उ and scope must be given to it. For had it been merely a repetition of the Tanadi Vanu, that root has already an indicatory उ so that letter need not have been repeated here. The conjugation is वनति and not वनुते । With a preposition we have प्रवनयति without lengthening. When the root does not take any preposition, it is optionally मित् and then the Causative is वनयति or वानयति । See Gana sutra ग्लास्नावनुवमां च lower down. The root Vanu means action in general. Pre. वनति । Per. ववान । I Fut. वनिता । Caus. प्रवनयति । Aor. अपीवनत् । Pass. Aor. अवनि or अवानि ॥
entries.sutra_ocr: वनु च ८४१ नोच्यते । 'वनु' इत्यपूर्व एवायं धातुर्न तु तानादिकस्यानुवादः । उदित्करणसामर्थ्यात् । तने क्रिया सामान्य वनतीत्यादि । प्रजनयति । अनुपसृष्टस्य तु मित्यविकल्पो बयते ॥

entries.english: 842. Jvala to shine. With this root also begins a sub-class called jvaladi which by III. 1. 140 take णा in forming verbal nouns, and it will be taught later on, see No. 884. That root, to be taught subsequently, is repeated here in order to make it मित् । As प्रज्वलयति । When it does not take a preposition it is optionally मित् । See Gana Sutra later down. Pre. ज्वलति । Caus. प्रज्वलयति । Pass. Aor. अज्वलि or अज्वालि ॥
entries.sutra_ocr: ज्वल ८४२ दीप्तौ । प्रत्ययार्थ पठिष्यमाणं एवायं मित्वार्थमाते । प्रस्वयति ॥

entries.english: 843. Hvala, 844 Hmala to walk, move. Pre. ह्वलति । Per. जाह्वल ।

I Fut. ‹?› । Aorist. ‹?› । There is no optional vṛiddhi, See VII. 2. 8. Caus. ‹?› । Without any preposition the root is optionally मित् । See below, Aorist Pass. ‹?› or ‹?› । Desi. ‹?› । Inten. ‹?› । Yaṅ luk ‹?›
entries.note: Continuation from page 193; tail of root 843.

entries.english: 844. Hmala, Pre. ‹?› Per. ‹?› । I Fut. ‹?› ॥
entries.note: Embedded Devanagari forms corrupt in OCR.

entries.english: 845. Smṛi. 'To remember with regret or anxiety.' This root is taught further on in the sense of 'remembering.' It is repeated here for the sake of making it मित् when it has the sense of remembering with regret. Adhyâna means 'remembering with anxiousness.' Pre. स्मरति । Caus. मातुः स्मरयति । Pass. Aor. अस्मारि or अस्मरि ॥

846. ✓ Dṛi to fear. Deva, Dhanapâla and Pūrṇa Chandra are of opinion that this is an original root. But Maitreya holds that it is the same root as ‹?› 'to burst' of the Kryâdi class No. 23 and that it is repeated here to give it the designation of मित् । This is the opinion endorsed by the author of Siddhânta. Thus the causative दरयति means ‹?› 'Causes to burst or split up'. When it has not the meaning of fear, we have दारयति । According to those who hold it to be a Bhvâdi root, it is conjugated as दरति &c. Some read this root as with a short ॠ in the sutra VII. 4. 95; 2566 instead of long. But that is wrong according to Mâdhava. Pre. दरति Per. ददार । दद्रतुः or ददरतुः । I Fut. दरिता । Caus. दरयति ॥

847. Nṛi to lead. This is a repetition of the root which will be taught in the Kryâdi class. When the meaning is not that of to lead the causative is नारयति । See Kryâdi No. 25. Pre. नरति or नरीति । Per. ननार । I Fut. नरिता । Aorist. अनारीत् । Caus. नरयति । Pass. Aor. अनरि or अनारी ॥

848. Śrâ, to cook. The ‹?› to cook will be taught later on. See No. 966. It is that root with its ‹?› changed to ‹?›, so that Śrâ may include both the Bhvâdi No. 966, and the Adâdi Śrâ No. 44. The following two Paribhâshâs should be remembered in connection with forms like these:—

Paribhâshâ 1.—If a root occurring in a rule be such that it belongs to two classes, one in which there is no elision of the characteristic (Vikaraṇa), and the other in which there is an elision of the vikaraṇa (such as the roots of the Adâdi class), then we must interpret the rule to mean the root which is not Adâdi. Thus ‹?› here belongs both to Bhvâdi and Adâdi; we must take it to mean Bhvâdi, and not Adâdi, in accordance with this maxim.

Paribhâshâ 2.—Whenever a term is employed which might denote both something original and also something else resulting from a rule of Grammar—or when a term is employed in a rule which might denote both something by another rule in which the same individual term has been employed, and also something else formed by a general rule—such a term should be taken to denote in the former case, only that which is original, and in the latter case, only that which is formed by that rule in which the same individual term has been employed. Thus in accordance with this maxim, the original root of the Adâdi class is to be taken, and not the root of the Bhvâdi class which assumes the form ‹?› by the application of a rule of Grammar. The combined result of these two maxims is that we take both roots—the ‹?› of Bhvâdi and the ‹?› of Adâdi. Thus the Caus. of ‹?› means 'causes to boil.' When not meaning to cook, we have ‹?› 'he causes to perspire.' Pre. ‹?› Per. ‹?› । I Fut. ‹?› । Caus. ‹?› । Aor. ‹?› or ‹?› ॥

849. ✓ Jñâ to kill, to satisfy, to observe or behold. According to Mâdhava, niśâmana means visual perception. Others say it means to inform in general. Another reading is Niśâneṣu. The root will then mean 'to sharpen'. The root ✓ Jñâ is मित् in these senses only. The Churâdi ✓ Jñâ is also मित् । See Churâdi No. 81. That also means to make known, to kill &c. If the root in these senses be मित्, how do you explain the forms विज्ञापयति and संज्ञापयति instead of विज्ञपयति and संज्ञपयति in the following sentences:—'विज्ञापना भर्तृषु सिद्धिमेति' 'Respectful statement made to superiors brings success,' or 'तज्ज्ञापयत्याचार्यः' 'thus announces or proclaims the Âchârya'? Listen. According to Mâdhava the Jñâ is मित् when it means seeing with eyes, and not intellectual conception. The root is therefore not मित् in the above examples, where it means to inform &c. and not visual perception. But in the opinion of those who hold the view that ✓ Jñâ is मित् in the sense of 'to see, to inform' in general, the above forms are explained by saying that they are derived from the ✓ Jñâ niyoge of the Churâdi class No. 193. For roots have many meanings; and so ✓ Jñâ is not confined to niyoga only. Of course, no such difficulties arise in the case of Haradatta and others who read निशानेषु 'to sharpen,' and not the ambiguous word निशामनेषु in the text.

NOTE:—The different meanings of this root are illustrated by the following examples. Thus पशुं संज्ञपयति 'He causes the sacrificial animal to be killed'; विष्णुं विज्ञपयति 'He propitiates Vishṇu'; संज्ञपयति रूपम् 'He shows the form' (according to Mâdhava), 'He explains the form' (according to others). प्रज्ञपयति शरम् 'He sharpens the arrow.'

850. Chali to shake. The 'Chala to shake' is a root belonging to the Jvalâdi sub-division. Thus चलयति शाखाम् 'He shakes the branch.' But when it does not mean to shake, the Causative is chalayati, as शीलं चालयति 'He deviates from good conduct. That is, he does what is not proper.' According to Svâmî it means 'to take away.' So also सूत्रं चालयति 'he throws the thread.' Here चालयति means क्षिपति according to Sudhâkara. Pre. चलति । Per. चचाल, चेलतुः, चेलुः । I Fut. चलिता ॥

851. Chhadir to strengthen, to animate. This is a repetition of the ✓ Chhada 'to cover over,' of the Churâdi class No. 290, without the णिच्, in order to make it a मित् root. As the roots have many meanings, the sense of ऊर्जन is attached to it here. Thus छदयति means 'he strengthens or animates.' In other senses, the causative is छादयति which means 'he causes to cover.' When the root is Churâdi and takes णिच् without change of sense, we have छादयति meaning 'he becomes strong,' 'he becomes animated' or 'he covers.'

852. Laḍi to loll the tongue. This is a repetition of the Laḍ 'to play' (see No. 381), in order to make it मित् when it has this particular sense. The word unmathana means 'to strike'. It forms with the word jihvâ a Genitive Tatpurusha compound meaning 'striking or shaking of the tongue.' Thus लडयति जिह्वाम् 'He lolls the tongue.' Or the word unmathana may form an Instrumental Tatpurusha compound with the word jihvâ. As लडयति जिह्वया 'He strikes by the tongue any other object.' Others hold that by the word jihvâ is indicated the action of the tongue. They say jihvonmathane is a Samâhâra Dvandva compound meaning 'the action of the tongue' and 'to strike'. Thus लडयति शत्रुम् 'He abuses the enemy'; and लडयति दधि 'he licks the curd or churns the curd.'
entries.note: Entry number misprinted as 850 in source heading; text cut off at end of page 196.

entries.english:
Note:—Thus for the purposes of मित् the root must mean (1) to loll the tongue, (2) to strike with the tongue, (3) to blame or abuse, (4) to lick &c. (any notion of the tongue) or to churn, or shake. When it has not these meanings, we have लाडयति पुत्रम् 'He fondles his son.'

Note:—Another reading is जिह्वामथनयोः । The word मथन is same as मन्थन. The ‹?› in the three roots वलि, ‹?› and लडि is not indicatory of नुम् augment, but merely marks the root.

मदी ८५३ हर्षग्लेपनयोः । ग्लेपनं दैन्यम् । वैवादिकस्य मित्त्वार्थोऽयमनुवादः । मदयति । हर्षयति । ग्लेपयति वेत्यर्थः । अन्यत्र मादयति । चित्तविकारमुत्पादयतीत्यर्थः ।

853. Madi 'to rejoice', 'to be poor'. Glepan means poverty. This is repetition of the Divadi root No. 99, for the sake of making it मित् । Thus मदयति means 'He causes to rejoice', or 'he causes to be poor.' When not denoting 'to rejoice or to be poor', we have मादयति 'It produces mental confusion.' So also विमादयति 'He pronounces the vowels and consonants clearly.' As we find in the Pratishakhyam उपलब्धिर्विमाद इति । अक्षरव्यञ्जनानामिति शेषः ॥

ध्वन ८५४ शब्दे । भाव्ययं मित्त्वार्थमन्वाद्यते । ध्वनयति घण्टाम् अन्यत्र—ध्वानयति । अस्पष्टाक्षरमुच्चारयतीत्यर्थः । अत्र भोजः 'दलि वलि स्खलि त्रपयः ध्वनि क्षपयश्च' इति पपाठ ।

854. Dhvana to sound. This is a repetition, for the sake of मित्, of the root No. 881 to be taught hereafter, see its conjugation there. Thus the Causative is ध्वनयति घण्टाम् 'He sounds the bell.' In any other sense we have ध्वानयति meaning 'He causes to articulate indistinctly.'

Here Bhoja adds the following seven roots also, namely, दलि, वलि, स्खलि, ध्वनि, त्रपि and क्षपि । Of these ध्वनि and रणि have already been mentioned before in this list see No. 854, and 832. The √ Dala to split (No. 581), √ Vala 'to cover' (No. 520), √ Skhala 'to stumble' (No. 577), and √ Trap 'to be ashamed' (No. 399), have already been taught before, though not in the मित् sub-division. The causatives of these will be दलयति, वलयति, स्खलयति and त्रपयति ॥

The root क्षपि is the same as the Kshai to waste, to be mentioned later on (see No. 961): the ऐ has been changed to अ and पुक् augment has been added. As क्षपयति ॥

तत्र ध्वनि ८५५ रणे उदाहृतौ ।

855. Rana to sound. Caus. रणयति ॥

दल विशरणे ८५६

856. Dala to split. Caus. दलयति ॥

वल संवरणे ८५७ ।

857. √ Vala, to cover. Caus. वलयति ॥

स्खल संचलने ८५८

858. Skhala to stumble. Caus. स्खलयति ॥

त्रपि ८५९, क्षपयश्च ८६० । त्रपुष् लज्जायाम् इति गताः । तेषां मित्वे दलति । वलयति । स्खलयति । त्रपयति । 'क्षै क्षये' इति वक्ष्यमाणस्य कृतात्त्वस्य पुका निर्देशः । क्षपयति ।

859. √ Trap to be ashamed. Caus. त्रपयति Cf. Trapush 399.

860. √ Kshai, to waste. Caus. क्षपयति with the पुक् augment.

स्वन ८६१ अवतंसने । शब्द इति पठिष्यमाणस्यानुवादः । स्वनयति । अन्यत्र स्वानयति ।

861. Svana, 'to adorn.' This is a repetition of the Svana 'to sound,' No. 879 to be taught later on. Thus the causative is स्वनयति 'He causes to adorn.' But in any other sense we have स्वानयति 'He causes to resound.'

घटादयो मितः । मित्संज्ञा इत्यर्थः ।

“Gana-sutra” A. The roots beginning with घट No. 800 and ending with स्वन (No. 861) are as if they had an indicatory म् ॥

The result of which is that sûtras VI. 4. 92. &c. apply to them. They get the designation मित् ॥

जन ८६२, जॄष ८६३, क्नसु ८६४, रञ्जो ८६५, अमन्ताः ८६६ ।
'मितः' इत्यनुवृत्तेः । 'जॄष' इति षित्वनिर्देशाज्जीर्यतेर्ग्रहणम् । जॄणातेस्तु जारयति । केचित्तु 'जनी जॄष्क्नसु' इति पठित्वा 'क्नसु निरसने' इति दाहरन्ति ।

“Gana sutra” B. The roots √ Jani, √ Jrish, √ Knasu, √ Ranja and those whose final is अम् are also मित् ॥

The word मित् is understood in this sûtra. The root is exhibited in the sûtra with an indicatory ष, as जॄष् ; and therefore it means the root जॄ that is conjugated as जीर्यति i. e. the Divadi जॄ. The Kryadi जॄ (जॄणाति) is not मित्, and its causative is जारयति । Some read this sûtra as, "The roots Jani, Jri, and √ Shnasu &c"; and they take the Divadi root Shnasu No. 5 and give example of it as ‹?› ॥

862. Jani 'to be produced.' It is a root of the Divadi class and is conjugated there. See No. 41. It being a मित्, the Causative is जनयति ॥

863. √ Jrish, 'to grow old.' This is also a Divadi root (see No. 22). Its causative is जरयति । Some read जॄ instead of जॄष् ॥

864. Knasu. This is also a Divadi root (see No. 6). The causative is क्नसयति ॥

865. Ranji 'to color.' This is a root belonging to both Divadi and Bhvadi classes. Its causative is रञ्जयति or रजयति । As रजति मृगान्—रमयति । The nasal is elided by the vartika under VI. 4. 91, ‹?› । No elision, as the object is 'birds' and not beasts.

866. The roots ending in अम् are मित् ॥

As the roots क्रम, गम्, शम, &c. Thus their causatives are क्रमयति, गमयति, शमयति ॥

ज्वलह्वलह्मलनभामनुपसर्गाद्वा । ८६७ । एषां मित्वं वा । प्राप्तविभाषेयम् । ज्वलयति । ज्वालयति । उपसृष्टे तु नित्यं मित्वम् । प्रज्वलयति । कथं तर्हि प्रज्वालयति । उद्नामयतीति । ण्यमन्तात् 'तत्करोति—' इति णिच् । कथं संक्रामयतीति । मितां ह्रस्वः' (२५६८) इति सूत्रे 'वा चित्तविरागे' (२६०१) इत्यतो 'वा' इत्यनुवृत्त्या व्यवस्थितविभाषाश्रयणादिति । एतेन 'रजो विश्रामयन्नब्जां' 'धुर्यान्विश्रामयेति सः' इत्यादि व्याख्यातम् ।

867. “Gana sutra” C. The roots √ Jvala, √ Hvala, √ Hmala, and √ Nama, are optionally मित् when not preceded by any preposition.

When they are not connected with a preposition they are optionally मित् । This is an example of prapta-vibhasha. For these roots have already been declared as मित् by the previous rules. नम ends in अम् and is मित् by the last sutra. The present sûtra declares an option under certain circumstances. As ज्वलयति or ज्वालयति ॥

But when they are preceded by an upasarga they are necessarily मित्, and no option is allowed. As प्रज्वलयति ॥

How do you explain the non-mit causatives like प्रज्वालयति and उद्नामयति ?

These are not from the roots ज्वल and नम, but from the nouns ज्वल and नमः formed by a added to the above roots. To the nouns ज्वल and नमः is added the Denominative affix णिच् with the force of तत्करोति । (See Churadi Gana sutra तत्करोति तदाचष्टे after the root कत्र) How do you explain the form संक्रामयति ? According to the author of Kasika Vritti, it is explained as an example of option. For he reads in the sûtra मितां ह्रस्वः (VI. 4. 92. S. 2568), the anuvritti of वा 'optionally' from वा चित्तविरागे (VI. 4. 91. S. 2601); and makes that rule a vyavasthita-vibhasha. On that theory is explained also the forms रजो विश्रामयन्नब्जां and धुर्यान्विश्रामयेति सः &c.

ग्लास्नावनुवमां च । ८६८ । अनुपसर्गादेषां मित्वं वा स्यात् । आद्ययोः अप्राप्तविभाषा । इतरयोः प्राप्तविभाषा ।

868. “Gana sûtra” D. The roots Gla, Sna, Vanu and Vama are optionally मित् when not preceded by any preposition.

These roots are optionally मित् when not preceded by any preposition. In the case of the first two roots, it is an aprapta-vibhasha, for no rule has as yet declared Gla and Sna as to be मित् । In the case of the last two roots, it is prapta-vibhasha, for they were already मित् by the previous sutra. Caus. ग्लापयति, ग्लापयति; स्नापयति, स्नापयति; वनयति, वानयति; वमयति, वामयति ॥

न कम्यमिवमाम् । ८६९ । अमन्तत्वात् प्राप्तं नित्यमेषां न स्यात् । कामयते । आमयति । चामयति ।

869. “Gana sutra” E. The roots √ Kam 'to love', √ Am 'to go' and √ Chamu 'to eat' are not मित् ॥

These roots all end in अम् and, therefore, by the Gana-sutra जनो &c. they would have been मित् । Thus Caus. कामयते । आमयति । चामयति ।

शमो दर्शने । ८७० । शाम्यतिर्दर्शने मिन् न स्यात् । निशामयति रूपम् । अन्यत्र तु "निशामय्य वधूकथाः" । कथं तर्हि "निशामय तदुत्पत्तिं विस्तराद् गदतो मम" दर्शनेऽपि । शम आलोचने दण्डादि चौरादिकस्य धातूनामनेकार्थत्वादत्र वृत्तिः शाम्यतिवत् ।
entries.note: Entry 2353 continues from previous page; contains Dhatupatha roots 853-870 under Ghatadi-gana without a new Panini sutra heading.

entries.english:
870. “Gaṇa-sûtra.” F. The root √ Sama meaning 'to see,' is not मित् ॥
This root belongs to the Divâdi class. As निशामयति रूपम् । 'He shows the form.' अत्युत्कृष्टमिदं तीर्थं भारद्वाजं निशामय । 'This is very excellent holy place; see it O! Bharadvâja!' When not meaning to see, it is मित्, as it ends with अम् । Thus प्रविश्य निशमय्य वधूः कथाः । How do you explain the form निशामय in the following verse: निशामय तदुत्पत्तिं विस्तराद् गदतो मम । 'Hear from me in detail the account of his birth.' This is a form of the Churâdi root √ शम् No. 156. As roots have multiple meanings, it means here 'to listen'; like शाम्यति ॥
यमोऽपरिवेषणे । ८७१ । यच्छतिर्भोजनतोऽन्यत्र मिन् न स्यात् । चायामयरित । द्राघयति । व्यापारयति वेत्यर्थः । परिवेषणे तु यमयति ब्राह्मणान् । 'भोजयति' इत्यर्थः । 'पर्यवसितं नियमयन्' इत्यादि तु नियमवच्छब्दात् ण्यन्तादिति बोध्यम् ।
871. “Gaṇa-sûtra.” G. The root √ yama, when not meaning to eat, is not मित् ॥
When not meaning to eat, the root यम उपरमे (यच्छति &c.), is not मित् । Thus चायामयरित which is equivalent to द्राघयति or व्यापारयति । But when it means 'to eat,' we have यमयति ब्राह्मणान् । 'He feeds the Brâhmaṇas.' The form नियमयन् is not the causative Present Participle of यम, but to the noun नियमवत् is added the Denominative affix णिच् under तत्करोति sûtra. When this affix is added, the वत् is elided. From the Denominative root thus formed, we get the Present Participle नियमयन् ॥
खदेर ८७२ अपरिभ्यां च । मित्त्वेत्येव । अवस्वादयति । परिस्वादयति । 'अपावपरिभ्यः' इति न्यासकारः । स्वामी तु 'न कमि-' इति नञं त्रिसूच्यामननुवर्त्य शमः 'आदर्शने' इति चिच्छेद । यमस्तु 'अपरिवेषणे' मित्त्वमाह । तन्मते 'पर्यवसितं नियमयन्' इत्यादि सम्यगेव । 'उपसृष्टस्य खदेरस्वेदनादिपूर्वस्य दर्शनं निपात्यस्वादयतीत्याह । तस्मात्सूत्रत्रये उदाहरणप्रत्युदाहरणयोर्व्यत्यासः फलितः । इदं च मतं वृत्तिन्यासाविविरोधादुपेक्ष्यम् ।
872. “Gaṇa-sûtra.” H. The root √ khada when preceded by the Prepositions 'ava' or 'pari' is not मित् ॥
The words 'it is not मित्' are understood here also. Thus अवस्वादयति and परिस्वादयति ॥
According to Bodhi Nyâsa, the three prepositions अप, अव and परि are taken for the purposes of this rule.
In the opinion of Svâmi the anuvṛitti of 'not' from the sûtra न कमि to Gaṇa-sûtra E is not to be read in the subsequent sûtras F, G, and H, as we have done. According to him the sûtra F is not शमो दर्शने but शमोऽदर्शने meaning the root √ शम् when denoting 'not-seeing' is मित् । He explains sûtra G as the root √ यम् when not meaning to eat is मित् । In his opinion the examples पर्यवसितं नियमयन् &c. are perfectly valid examples under the rule, with nothing exceptional about them. With regard to the present sûtra H, he explains it by saying “the √ khada which is always मित् without a preposition, is conditionally मित्, when preceded by the Prepositions अव, and परि but it is not मित्, when preceded by any other Preposition than these two.” In other words he makes the present sûtra a Niyama rule, restricting the मित्-hood of the compound verb √ Skhada to the Prepositions अव and परि । Therefore प्रस्वादयति is not मित्, because the upasarga is प्र । Thus of the three sûtras F, G and H, as regards F, there is no ultimate difference between the Swâmi and us. With regards to G and H his view is diametrically opposed to us; so that the examples we have given under these sûtras are his counter-examples, and our counter-examples are his examples. This opinion should be rejected as opposed to the author of the Kâśikâ Vṛitti, and Nyâsakâra &c.
फण ८७३ गतौ । 'न' इति निवृत्तमसंभवात् । निषेधात्पूर्वमसो पठितः । फणादिकार्यानुरोधात् ।
873. Phaṇa, to go. The anuvṛitti of न of the Gaṇa-sûtra E which was current in the previous sûtras, is not to be read in this, and its anuvṛitti ceases; for it is not possible to read it into this sûtra. This sûtra could well have been inserted prior to the commencement of the prohibitory sûtras E, F, G, H. But it has not been so read, because of the necessity of those rules which ordain specific operations with regards to Phaṇâdi roots such as the next sûtra.
entries.note: Tail continuation of SK 2353 covering Gana-sutras F, G, H and root 873 Phana.

entries.english:
2354. ए is optionally substituted for the अभ्यास and आकार of the seven roots फण, राज्, भ्राज्, भ्राश्, भ्लाश्, स्यम् and स्वन and the reduplicate is elided thereby, before the affixes of the Perfect having an indicatory क् (or ङ्) as well as before the थ with iṭ augment.
Thus फेणतुः, फेणुः, फेणिथ or पफणतुः, पफणुः, पफणिथ ॥ So also the causative फाणयति ॥
वृत् । घटादिः समाप्तः । फणेः प्रागेव वृदित्येके । तन्मते फाणयतीत्येव ।
End. The word vṛit means that the Ghaṭâdi roots end here or they remain only upto this place. It marks the end of this sub-division. Some read this word वृत् just before फण; and so in their opinion it is not a मित् root. Their causative is फाणयति ॥
Pre. फणति । Per. पफाण । फेणतुः । फेणुः । पफणिथ or फेणिथ । पफणथ । पफण or फेण । पफणिम or फेणिम । I Fut. फणिता । Aorist अपाणीत् । अफणीत् । Caus. फाणयति । Caus. Aor. अपिफणत् । When not meaning to go, we have फाणयति सक्तून् 'He skims the gruel.' Desi. पिफणिषति । Inten. पंफण्यते । Yaṅ luk. पम्फणीति or पम्फाणीति । D. पम्फाणीतः । Imperative पम्फाहि । Noun फाणितः 'a decoction.'
राज् ८७४ दीप्तौ । स्वरितेत् । राजति - राजते । रेजतुः - रराजतुः 'धातवेकाचः' इत्यनुवृत्तावपि विधानसामर्थ्यादात एत्वम् ।
874. Râjṛi to shine. It is svaritet and consequently is conjugated in both Padas. Its enumeration in the preceding root No. 194 is to prevent the application to it of the ष rule VIII. 2. 36. The आ of that भ्राज् is not changed to ए; but the अ of this bhrâj is so changed. For in the sûtra VIII. 2. 36 the root bhrâj is read in the company of राज् and so indicates that it is the Phaṇâdi √ Bhrâj which is the subject of that rule. 'स्यमू ८७८, स्वन ८७९, ष्टन or स्तन ८८०, ध्वन ८८१ शब्दे' । स्यमादयः क्षम्यन्ताः परस्मैपदिनः । स्येमतुः - सस्यमतुः । अस्यामीत् । स्वेरतुः - सस्वनतुः । सस्वनुः । अस्वानोत् अस्वनीत् । विष्यति । सिद्धं भुङ्क्ते इत्यर्थः । 'वेञ् स्वनः-' (२३०५) इति षत्वम् । फणाद्येकाचः । दध्वनतुः ॥

entries.english:
2355. The augment प् is added after the vowel of the root पत in the अङ् Aorist.
अपप्तत्, अपप्तताम्, अपप्तन् । The पत takes the अङ् Aorist as it has an indicatory ॡ in the Dhatupatha (III. 1. 55).
The न of the upasarga नि is changed to ण after an alterant preposition by S. 2285. As न्यपप्तत् ।

कथ ८९९ निष्पाके । क्वथति । चक्वाथ । अक्वथीत् ॥

899. Kvatha to boil, decoct, digest. Pre. क्वथति । Per. चक्वाथ । I Fut. क्वथिता । Aorist अक्वथीत् । Caus. क्वाथयति । It belongs to the Ghatadi class and hence मित् । Noun क्वाथः ॥

पथे ९०० गतौ । अपथीत् ॥

900. Pathe to go. Pre. पथति । Per. पपाथ । पेथतुः । I Fut. पथिना । Aorist अपथीत् । Noun पथः । पाथः ॥

मथे ९०१ विलोडने । मेथतुः । अमथीत् ॥

901. Mathe to churn. Pre. मथति । Per. ममाथ । मेथतुः । I Fut. मथिता । Aorist अमथीत् । Nouns माथः । मथः ॥

टुवम् ९०२ उद्गिरणे । इहैव निपातनात् ऋतः इदिति सुधाकरः । ववाम । ववमतुः । ववादित्वादेत्वाभ्यासलोपो न । भागवृत्तौ तु वेमतुरित्याद्यप्युदाहृतं तद्भाष्यादौ न दृष्टम् ॥

902. Tuvama, to vomit.
The word उद्गिरणे is from the root गृ । The short ऋ could not be changed to इ by any rule of Grammar. The grammatical form would have been उद्गरणम् with the Guna of ऋ । But Panini uses the word उद्गिरणे in this sûtra. So Sudhakara says "the Nipâtana of this sûtra is the authority for changing the short ऋ of गृ into इ।" Pre. वमति । Per. ववाम । ववमतुः । There is no एत्व or the elision of abhyasa, because the root begins with व ।
In Bhagavritti the forms वेमतुः &c. are given. They are not found in the Bhashya &c. I Fut. वमिता । Aorist अवामीत् । No Vriddhi. Caus. वामयति, वमयति । See Gana sutra ‹?› of the Ghatadi. Desi. विवमिषति । Inten. वावम्यते । Yan luk वावमीति । d. वंवंः । Imperative ववांहि । Imperfect अववन् । Past Part. Pass. वान्तः । Act. वान्तवान् । Nouns वामः । वमथुः ॥

भ्रमु ९०३ चलने । 'वा भ्राश' (२३२१) इति श्यन्वा । भ्राम्यति-भ्रमति । 'भ्राम्यति' इति तु दिवादावेष्यते ॥

903. Bhramu to move, to walk.
This root is optionally conjugated as a Divadi root with श्यन् Vikarana (See 2321). Thus भ्राम्यति or भ्रमति । The form भ्राम्यति will be taught later on in the Divadi. The Perfect is बभ्राम ।
In forming its dual the following sûtra applies.

entries.english:
2356. e is optionally substituted for the a of the stems जृ (ऋ), भ्रम, and त्रस् and the reduplicate is thereby elided, before the affixes of the Perfect having an indicatory क् (or ङ्), as well as before the थल् with the augment इट् ॥

Thus (जेरतुः, जेरुः, जेरिथ, or जजरतुः, जजरुः, जजरिथ) भेमतुः, भेमुः, भेमिथ, or बभ्रमतुः, बभ्रमुः, बभ्रमिथ । त्रेसतुः, त्रेसुः, त्रेसिथ, or तत्रसतुः, तत्रसुः, तत्रसिथ ॥

903. Bhramu to move, to walk. क्षर ९०४ संचलने । अक्षारीत् ॥

904. Kshara, to ooze, to flow. Some read this sûtra as क्षल संचलने । 'चल' is conjugated like क्षर । Pre. क्षरति । Per. चक्षार । I Fut. क्षरिता । Aorist अक्षारीत् । Desi. चिक्षरिषति । Inten. चाक्षर्यते । Yan-luk चाक्षर्ति । Imperative चाक्षर्हि । Imperfect अचाक्षर् । Nouns: क्षारः । क्षरः । क्षरेजः ॥

Here end the roots beginning with Sama, which were Udātta and Udāttet.

SUB-SECTION.

अथ द्वावनुदात्तेत्तौ ॥

Now the next two roots are Anudātteta.

षह ९०५ मर्षणे । परिनिविभ्य (२३७५) इति षत्वम् । परिषहते । सेहे ॥

सहिता । 'तीषसह-' (२३४०) इति वा इट् । इडभावे ढत्वधत्वष्टुत्वढलोपाः ॥

905. √Shaha to endure, forbear.

The Perfect is सेहे ।

The स is changed to ष by VIII. 3. 70, S. 2375 when preceded by pari, vi, or ni. As परिषहते ।

The first future सहिता । The इट् augment is optional by VII. 2. 48, S. 2340. When इट् is not added, then we have the equation: सह् + ता = सद् + ता (VIII. 2. 31, S. 321) = सढ् + धा (VIII. 2. 40, S. 2280) = सढ् + ढा (VIII. 4. 40, S. 111) = स + ढा (VIII. 3. 13, S. 2335).

Now applies VI. 3. 112, S. 2357 by which the अ of स is changed to ओ ॥

2357. When ढ or ढ्र are elided, there is the substitution of ओ for the अ or आ of the verbs सह and वह ॥

Thus स + ढा = सोढा ॥

This स of Soḍha however is not changed to ष after परि &c., because of the following sûtra:—
entries.note: Sutra number misprinted as २३५० in OCR.

entries.english:
2358. The स of सोढ form of the root सह is not changed to ष after परि &c. As परिसेाढा । This is an exception to VIII. 3. 70.

Note:—Why do we say 'when सह assumes the form of सोढ' । Observe परिसहते, विषहते ॥

The change of स to ष of √सह is optional by the following sûtra when the augment intervenes between the verb and the preposition परि &c.
entries.note: Panini reference misprinted as ५.३.११५ in OCR for 8.3.115; entry spans across page boundary to 207.

entries.english:
2359. The ष-change may take place optionally in the सिवादी and the rest (of sûtra VIII. 3. 70 S. 2275), even when the augment intervenes between the prepositions परि, नि or वि and the verb.

The सिवादी are the four roots सिव्, षिद्, सह, and ष्वञ्ज, as well as the augment सुट् । This is an example of ubhayatra-vibhāshā. In the case of ष्वञ्ज it is prāpta-vibhāshā, in the case of others it is aprāpta. Thus परि + असह (Imperfect) = पर्यषहत or पर्यसहत ॥

S. सासक्षि । Adjective सह्यम् । Nouns: साहः । सहः । सहिष्णुः । सहनः । सासहिः ॥

रमु ९०६ क्रीडायाम् । रेमे । रेमिषे । रन्ता । रंस्यते । रंसीष्ट । अरंस्त ॥

SUB-SECTION.

अथ कसन्ताः परस्मैपदिनः ।

The roots up to घास are Parasmaipadi.

षदॢ ९०७ विशरणगत्यवसानेषु ।

907. √Shadḷr. 1. To split or burst, 2. to go, 3. to be dejected. In conjugating this root, सद् is replaced by सीद by the following sûtra:—
entries.note: Sutra number misprinted as २३९ in OCR.

entries.english:
2360. Before a Present-character (शित्), the following substitutions take place:—पिब् for पा, जिघ्र for घ्रा, धम for ध्मा, तिष्ठ for स्था, मन for मन्, यच्छ for दा (दाण्), पश्य for दृश्, ऋच्छ for ऋ, धौ for सृ, शीय for शद् and सीद for सद् ॥

Thus we have सीदति in the Present. The Perfect is ससाद, सेदतुः । सेदिथ or ससत्थ । The First Future is सत्ता । The Second Future is सत्स्यति । The Aorist is formed by अङ्, as the root has an indicatory ऌ (ḷṛ) as असदत् ॥

The स is changed to ष when preceded by an alterant Preposition except प्रति (VIII. 3. 66 S. 2271) as निषीदति and न्यषीदत् । But the स coming after the reduplicate is not so changed because the following applies:—

2361. The स of सद् after the reduplicate in the Perfect is not changed to ष.

In the Perfect, when root is reduplicated, there are two स's, as ससाद । After a preposition, the first स will be changed to ष, but not so the second. Thus अभिषसाद, परिषसाद, निषसाद, विषसाद । Pre. सीदति । Per. ससाद, सेदतुः । 2. S. ससत्थ or सेदिथ । 1. d. सेदिव । 1. pl. सेदिम । I Fut. सत्ता । II Fut. सत्स्यति । Imperative सीदतु । Imper. असीदत् । Poten. सीदेत् । Bene. षद्यात् । Aorist असदत् । Caus. सादयति । Aor. असीषदत् । Desi. सिषत्सति । Inten. सेषिद्यते । Yan-luk साषत्ति । Per. Part. Parasmai. सेदिवान् । Nouns: परिषद् । सत्रः । सादः । निषादः । सत्रं । सद्धम् ॥

शद्लृ ९०८ शातने । विशीर्णतायामयम् । शातनं तु विषयतया निर्दिश्यते ॥

908. √Shadḷṛ, to fall, perish, decay, wither. The root means to decay. Here Maitreya has the following: “The root shadḷṛ means rending asunder (विशातन). The root has the meaning of decay. The form शातने however is given as its meaning and not विशीर्णतायाम्, because शातन is derived from this very root shad with ल्युट् affix, and is a well-known word.” This root, however, is Ātmanepadi before sit affixes by the following:—
entries.note: Sutra number misprinted as २०६१ in OCR.

entries.english:
2362. After the verb शद् to decay, when it has one of the affixes with an indicatory श (śit) the Ātmanepada is used.

Note:—The root 'shad' when taking any affix which is marked with an indicatory श, is conjugated in the Ātmanepadi. In connection with this, must be read sûtra VII. 3. 78, S. 2360 पाघ्राध्मास्था... by which the root शद् is replaced by शीय before affixes having an indicatory श । Thus शद् + श + ते = शीय + ते = शीयते 'he decays or withers,' शीयेते 'they two decay,' शीयन्ते 'they decay.' Pre. शीयते । Per. शशाद, शेदतुः । शेदिथ or शशत्थ । शेदिव । I Fut. शत्ता । II Fut. शत्स्यति । Imperative शीयताम् । Imper. अशीयत । Poten. शीयेत । Bene. शत्सीष्ट । Aorist अशदत् । Caus. शातयति । Desi. शिशात्सति । Inten. शेशीद्यते । Yan-luk शाशत्ति । Nouns: शादः । शातनम् । शद्मः । शत्रुः ॥

entries.english:
2364. For the penultimate short u of the guṇated stem (from गुह्), there is substituted long û before an affix beginning with a vowel.
Thus गुह् + शप् + ति = गोह् + अ + ति = गूह् + अ + ति = गूहति । Âtmanepada गूहते ।
In the First Future the iṭ augment is optional, as the root has an indicatory long ऌ (VII. 2. 44). Thus गूहिता or गोढा । So also in the Second Future, as गूहिष्यति or घोक्ष्यति । The Potential is गूहेत् । The Benedictive is गुह्यात् । The Aorist is अगूहीत् । But when it does not take iṭ, we have क्स, and then the form is अधुक्षत् ॥
In the Âtmanepada, this क्स is optionally elided by the following.

2365. The whole of the affix क्स is elided optionally before the personal endings of the Âtmanepada beginning with a dental, after दुह्, दिह्, लिहू and गुह् ॥
Thus अगूह् + क्स + त = अगूह् + 0 + त = अगूढ् + त (VIII. 2. 31. S. 324) = अगूढ् + ध (VIII. 2. 40 S. 2280) = अगूढ् + ढ (VIII. 4. 41. S. 111) = अगू + ढ (VIII. 3. 13. S. 2335) = अगूढ (VI. 3. 111. S. 174.)
The other form is अधुक्षत । Before the dual आताम् the final of क्स is elided by S. 2337 and we have the form अधुक्षाताम् । The Plural similarly is अधुक्षन्त । The 1st Person dual is अगूह्वहि or अधुक्षावहि । The Plural is अगूह्महि or अधुक्षामहि ॥
Note:— As अदुग्ध or अधुक्षत, अदुग्धाः or अधुक्षथाः, अदुग्ध्वम् or अधुक्षध्वम्, अदुह्वहि or अधुक्षावहि, अदिग्ध or अधिक्षत, अलीढ or अलिक्षत, न्यगूढ or न्यधुक्षत ॥
Why दुह् &c. only? Observe व्यत्यकृत । Why in the Âtmanepada? Observe अधुक्षत् only. Why before an affix beginning with a dental? Observe अधुक्षामहि only.
Though the anuvṛitti of लोप was understood in this sûtra, the employment of the term लुक् indicates that the whole of the affix is to be elided. For लोप would have elided only the final अ of क्स । But even with the elision of अ alone we would have got all the above forms, except those in वहि । For स् being elided, we have स् between (a consonant of झल् class) and a dental (which is also a letter of झल् class). This स् situate between two झल् will be elided by VIII. 2. 26. Nor can it be objected that the elided अ is sthânivat, for by पूर्वत्रासिद्धम् VIII. 2. 1, such an

elision cannot be sthānivat. Though य् is a dento-labial, yet it is included in the word dental. Had it not been meant to be so included, ‹?› would have been taken in the sūtra. See III. 1. 45, for this Aorist-affix.

2366. स्य the sign of the Future and Conditional gets the augment इट्, after a root ending in short ऋ and after हन्.

Thus भरिष्यति । In forming the Benedictive the following sūtra applies :
2367. For the final short of a root, there is substituted रिङ्, before the Present-character (‹?›), before the Passive-character, य, and before the augment ‹?› in the Benedictive.

2372. The final ‹?› of a root is elided before an Ārdhadhātuka affix with the augment ‹?› as well as when it begins with a vowel and has an indicatory ‹?›. Thus दा + अतुस् ।

Here the rule of elision (VI. 4. 64, § 2372) is subsequent in the Ashṭādhyāyī order to the rule of doubling (VI. 1. 1. and 8. § 2175 and 2177), hence elision ought to take place first and then doubling. But this is prevented by § 2213. We double the root first and then elide the ‹?›. Thus the dual is ददतुः । Pl. ददुः । 2nd S. ददाथ or ददिथ । 1st d. ददिव ॥

The First Future is दाता । In forming the Benedictive the following two sūtras apply.

entries.english:
2373. The verbs having the form of dā 'to give' and dhā 'to place,' are called ghu.

NOTE:—This defines the word ghu. Four verbs have the form of dā, or assume it by the application of VI. 1. 45, § 2370 and two, of dhā; they are called ghu. The ghu verbs have certain peculiarities of conjugation to be described hereafter. The verbs are the following :—डुदाञ् 'to give,' as प्रणिददाति ; देङ् 'to give,' as प्रणिदयते ; दो 'to cut,' as प्रणिद्यति ; दैप् 'to pity,' as प्रणिदायते ; डुधाञ् 'to place,' as प्रणिदधाति ; धेट् to 'suck' as प्रणिधयति । In these examples, because of the verbs being ghu, the न् of प्रणि is changed into ण् by VIII. 4. 17.

Similarly दाप् 'to cut' and दैप् 'to clean' not being called ghu, rules VII. 4. 46 and 47 do not apply to them. Thus दाप् + क्त = 'what is cut,' as अवदातः । So also दैप् 'washed' as 'a bright face.' But with दा 'to give,' &c. दा + त = दत् + त (VII. 4. 46) = दत्तः 'given,' so also we have + = दत्तम् (VII. 4. 47). The word ghu occurs in sūtra VI. 4. 66, &c. The word dāp includes also daip by the paribhāshā given under III. 4. 19, changed into दा by VI. 1. 45, § 2370.

The root having got the designation ghu, now applies the next sūtra.

2374. ए is substituted for the आ of the above roots in the Benedictive mood Active.

NOTE:—Thus देयात्, मेयात्, धेयात्, स्थेयात्, गेयात्, पेयात्, and अवसेयात् । Before non-कित् and non-ङित् we have ‹?›. By the word लिङ् is here meant the यासुँट्लिङ् or the Precative mood; the Personal endings of which mood are ārdhadhātuka by III. 4. 116. Moreover by III. 4. 104 the Parasmaipada affixes only of the Benedictive are कित्, so the present rule does not apply to the Ātmanepada affixes of the Precative.

Thus धा + यात् = धेयात् । D. धेयास्ताम् । Pl. धेयासुः ॥

In forming the Aorist there is optionally ‹?› by the following.

2375. After the roots धेट् 'to suck,' and श्वि, 'to grow,' is optionally the substitute of च्लि, when लुङ् follows signifying an agent.

As, अदधत् 'he sucked,' dual अधताम् । The reduplication is by § 2312. When it takes the alternative सिच्, then the next sūtra, III. 1. 44 § 2376 comes into operation, and we have अधात् and अधासीत् 'he sucked.' So also of श्वि, we have अशिश्वियत्, 'he grew.' It also takes the अङ्, (III. 1. 58) and then its form is अश्वत् ॥

2376. After the verbs घ्रा 'to smell,' धेट् 'to drink,' शो 'to pare,' छो (छे) 'to cut,' and सो (सो) 'to destroy' there is optionally the elision of सिच्, when parasmaipada terminations are employed.

Thus we have अधात् । d. अधाताम् । Pl. अधुः । When सिच् is not elided, the following applies.

NOTE:—Thus (अघ्रात्, or अध्रासीत् 'he smelled') अधात्, or अधासीत् 'he drank;' अशात्, or अशासीत् 'he pared;' अच्छात् or अच्छासीत् 'he cut' and असात्, or असासीत् 'he destroyed.' There is no option allowed in Ātmanepada; thus, ‹?› ।

The root धेट् is a Ghu verb, and in its case, the सिच् would have been elided by the last rule also. The present declares an option.

2377. The सिच् of the Aorist in the Parasmaipada takes the augment इट् after यम्, रम्, नम् and roots ending in long आ, and स् (सक्) is added at the end of these stems.

Thus अधासीत् । D. अधासिष्टाम् । Pl. अधासिषुः ॥

NOTE:—Thus अयंसीत् अयंसिष्टाम् अयंसिषुः । व्यरंसीत् । व्यरंसिष्टाम् । व्यरंसिषुः । The root रम् is Parasmaipadī when preceded by वि or आ (I. 3. 83). अनंसीत्, अनंसिष्टाम्, अनंसिषुः । Of roots ending in long आ:—अयासीत् । अयासिष्टाम् ; अयासिषुः । ‹?› When the conjugation is Ātmanepadī, the rule does not apply. As आयस्त अरंस्त । अनंस्त ॥

The Vṛiddhi in the case of यम् so ordained by VII. 2. 3, does not take place by VII. 2. 4. In the Ātmanepada we have आयस्त. The root यम् is Ātmanepadī, as it is preceded by आ (I. 3. 75). अरंस्त, अनंस्त (III. 1. 86). Exception to VII. 2. 10.

2378. For the final of any other root than those mentioned in VI. 4. 66, ए may optionally be substituted, in the Benedictive active, when the root begins with a conjunct consonant.

The स्था was the only root of VI. 4. 66, which could have been affected by this rule. It has been, however, specially exempted by the word अन्यस्य । Thus ग्लेयात्, or ग्लायात्, म्लेयात्, or म्लायात्, but only स्थेयात् (VI. 4. 66), and यायात् (not commencing with a double consonant). The phrase कित् is understood here and therefore the rule applies to Parasmaipada affixes (III. 4. 104). Thus ग्लासीष्ट in Ātmanepada. The root considered as an aṅga, should consist of a double consonant, therefore in निर्यायात् (from निर् + या), निर्या is not to be considered as a root having a double consonant, for र् is no part of the aṅga, but of the preposition.

entries.english: 2379. A root ending in short ऋ and preceded by a conjunct consonant gets Guṇa in the Perfect. Though this rule is primarily for the sake of कित् affixes even, yet being subsequent it applies to णल् also. By I. 2. 5. S. 2242, the affixes of the Perfect, other than णल् are कित् and consequently would not have caused Guṇa. This sûtra prevents that. Then comes the question, does this sûtra prevent the Vṛiddhi of णल् । According to the Kāśikā, it does not debar the Vṛiddhi of णल् caused by VII. 2. 115 S. 254. But according to the Siddhānta the present sûtra VII. 4. 10. being subsequent in order of the Ashṭādhyāyī to the Vṛiddhi sûtra, VII. 2. 115 S. 254. applies to that latter also. Thus we get hvṛi + ṇal = hvar + ṇal (Guṇa caused by the present sûtra) = hvar + ṇal (I. 1. 51 S. 51) = hvār + ṇal (there is Vṛiddhi of the penultimate by VII. 2. 116. S. 2282) = जह्वार । Dual जह्वरतुः । Pl. जह्वरुः । 2nd S. जह्वर्थ । First Future ह्वर्ता । In the Second Future there is इट् augment by VII. 2. 70. S. 2366. Thus we have ह्वरिष्यति ॥ In forming the Benedictive, the following sûtra causes Guṇa :—

entries.english: 2381. The augment इट् is not added to an affix having an indicatory क् or ङ् when it comes after the root श्रि, or after a monosyllabic root ending in an उक् in the Dhātupāṭha. This sûtra VII. 2. 11. is prior in Ashṭādhyāyī order to the sûtra स्वरतिसूति &c. VII. 2. 44, S. 2279 that ordains option; but nevertheless it debars that option: because this rule occurs in the general section of prohibition of इट् which commences with नेड् वशि कृति (VII. 2. 8) and is prior to the ordinance of VII. 2. 35. The present sûtra, therefore, would have totally debarred इट् as in the Nishṭhā स्वृतः, सूतः &c. The augment however is added compulsorily in the Perfect, by the restrictive rule of Krādi (VII. 2. 13. S. 2293) for स्वृ is not within the general exception of that rule. Thus we get सस्वरिव and सस्वरिम ॥ In the Second Future there is compulsory इट् augment by VII. 2. 70. S. 2366. entries.english:
2382. After the verbs 'to go,' 'to order,' and 'to go,' ‹?› is the substitute of ‹?› in the Parasmaipada as well as in the Atmanepada.

NOTE:—Thus, ‹?› 'he went;' ‹?› 'he ordered'; with ‹?› 'he went.' This sutra has been separately enunciated in order to make the rule applicable to Atmanepada; as व्यगाष्ट (1. 2. 29). The च in the text is for the sake of drawing the anuvritti of the phrase 'in the Parasmaipada' of the last sutra, into the present and its anuvritti will extend to future sutras also.
The roots ‹?› and ‹?› here being read along with the elided root ‹?›, mean the Juhotyadi roots ‹?› and ‹?› and not the ‹?› and ‹?› of the Bhvadi class. Therefore in the Bhvadi there is no ‹?› Aorist.

2383. There is guna in the Perfect of ‹?› of the Tudadi class, and of ‹?› and roots ending in long ‹?›

NOTE:—As आनर्च, आनर्च्छतुः, आनर्च्छुः from ऋच्छ; आर, आरतुः, आरुः from ऋ, and ‹?› from ॠ and not having light vowel in the penultimate, would not have received guna by VII. 3. 86, this sutra ordains it; roots in long ॠ never receive guna, but substitution; this ordains guna.
The Vriddhi of VII. 2. 115 supersedes this rule, within its own jurisdiction, a prior superseding the posterior as ‹?›
Thus ‹?› + ‹?› = ‹?› + ‹?› ।
Now there is Vriddhi of the penultimate by VII. 3. 116, and with reduplication we get ‹?› । Thus 3rd. S. ‹?› । D. ‹?› । Pl. ‹?› ॥

2384. The affix gets always the augment after and

NOTE:—As ‹?›, ‹?›, and ‹?› । The root is not changed to ‹?› (VI. 1. 46) in the Perfect. By VII. 2. 63, the roots ऋ and व्ये would have optionally been सेट्, and ‹?› never; therefore, the present sutra makes the इट् augment compulsory. The ‹?› is repeated in the aphorism for the sake of clearness, the rule could have stood without it, for the anuvritti of 'optionally' could not have run into it from the last sutra: for if it was an optional sutra, the enumeration of ऋ and व्ये was useless, as they were already provided for by VII. 2. 63.
