entries.english:
2386. And sri is the substitute of sru, and there is the affix snu after it, when a sarvadhatuka affix denoting an agent, follows.

This debars the Bhu-class vikarana sap. As the vikarana snu is nit (as it has no indicatory p, I. 2. 4), there is no guna of the vowel of the root.
Thus sru + snu + tip = sri + nu + ti = srinoti 'he hears'; srinutah 'they two hear.'
In forming the plural, the following sutra applies.

2387. The semi-vowel is substituted for the u of hu, and for that of snu (the characteristic of the fifth class roots), before a sarvadhatuka affix (III. 4. 113) beginning with a vowel, when the stem consists of more than one syllable and the u is not preceded by a conjunct consonant.

NOTE:—Thus srinvanti, srinvah; srinvathah so also with su—as sunvanti, sunvah, sunvan. Why do we say 'of hu and snu formed stems'? Observe yoyuvati, erati from Intensive bases, by the elision of the affix. The elided is in the
entries.note: Entry commentary cut off at bottom of p. 226 / batch end.

entries.english:
secular literature also, by the implication (jñāpaka) of this aphorism, for no counter-example can be formed of a root consisting of more than one syllable and ending in u, not preceded by a conjunct consonant and followed by a Sārvadhātuka affix, unless the Intensive roots with the elision of yaṅ be taken. Nor can we get examples from the Chhandas, for the preceding rule applies only to ārdhadhātuka affixes. Why do we say before a Sārvadhātuka? Observe जुहुवतुः, जुहुवुः (VI. 4. 77). So also not in ‹?› and ‹?›, as the u is preceded by a conjunct consonant.
This debars the उवङ् substitute. Thus ‹?› = शृण्वन्ति (and not शृणुवन्ति).

998. Gāñ, to go. It is thus conjugated. गा + शप् + ते ... In the dual गा + शप् becomes by coalescence गाते for the rule of सवर्णदीर्घः being antaranga applies first, and so the rule VII. 2. 81. S. 2235 finds no scope, for there remains no longer any आ which is a portion of a ङित् affix. The plural is गा + शप् + झ = गाते (VII. 1. 5. S. 2268) = गाते । In the First Person Singular the affix is changed to ए, and we have गा + शप् + इट् = गा + ए = गै ॥
In the First Person Imperfect we have अ + गा + इ = अगै by VI. 1. 87. S. 69.
The Benedictive is गासीष्ट । The sutra गाङ्कुटादिभ्यः (S. 2461) refers to that गा which is the substitute of इण् ; and not to this गाङ् । Therefore this गाङ् is not ङित्, and consequently the sūtra घुमास्था &c. (S. 2462) does not apply, and so there is no ई । In other words the form is not गेयास्त ।

2390. For the final long ऋ of a root, there is substituted ‹?› (I. 1. 51).

Note:— As किरति, गिरति from कॄ and गॄ of the Tudādi class. विस्तीर्णम् from स्तॄ, the lengthening is by VIII. 2. 77. Why do we say of a root? Observe ‹?›. This substitution will apply to Derivative roots also, as ‹?› from कॄ 'to scatter.'

Thus तॄ + शप् + ति = तिर् + अ + ति । Now applies the following.

Vârttika:— The rules of ‹?› and उ are set aside by the rules of guṇa and vṛiddhi, on the maxim that the subsequent debars a preceding rule. The general rule that a subsequent debars a precedent would not have applied here, because the rule being antaraṅga is stronger than the guṇa rule. Hence the necessity of this vârttika. Therefore we have तॄ + शप् + ति = तर् + शप् + ति (Guṇa) = तरति ।

2394. The affix सन् comes after the verbs मान 'to honor,' बध 'to bind,' दान 'to cut' and शान 'to whet', and long is the substitute of the i (VII. 4. 79) of the reduplicative (VI. 1. 4) syllable.

This affix is to be added to the above verbs when they have the following meaning ✓ Gup to 'despise,' ✓ Tij 'to endure' and ✓ Kit 'to heal,' 'to curb,' 'to remove,' 'to destroy,' 'to doubt,' ✓ Mân 'to ask,' ✓ Badh 'to loathe,' ✓ Dân 'to straighten,' ✓ Sân 'to whet' according to the following vârttikas :—

Vârtika :—The affix san is added to ✓ Gup when it has the sense of to blame or despise.

Vârtika :—The affix san is added to ✓ Tij when it means 'to forbear.'

Vartika :—The affix san is added to ✓ Kit when it means 'to heal,' 'to restrain or punish,' 'to remove,' 'to destroy,' 'to doubt.'

Vartika :—The affix san is added to ✓ Mân when it means 'to ask.'

Vârtika :—The affix san is added to ✓ Badh when it means mental perturbation.

Vartika :—The affix san is added to ✓ Dân when it means to straighten.

Vârtika :—The affix san is added to ✓ Sân when meaning 'to sharpen.'

The stems ending in सन् &c. are dhâtus or roots by S. 2304. When सन् is added there is reduplication by the following.

2395. Of a non-reduplicate root ending in सन् (Desiderative) or यङ् (Intensive) affixes, there is reduplication of the first syllable if it begins with a consonant, and of the second syllable if the root begins with a vowel.

NOTE:—The word सन्यङोः should be construed as genitive dual and not as Locative dual. In the latter case, the meaning would be "when the affixes सन् and यङ् follow, a non-reduplicate root is reduplicated." The difficulty would be that while the root alone would be reduplicated, the augment would not, as in टिटविषति, अशिशिषति । The phrase धातोरनभ्यासस्य is understood here also. The reduplication is of the first or second syllable, according as the root has an initial consonant or vowel. Thus पच् + सन् (III. 1. 7) पक्ष, reduplicate पिपक्षति (VII. 4. 79).

The roots Gup &c., with the exception of ✓ Kit, when having the senses of 'despising' &c. are anudâtteta and not otherwise. The roots ✓ Dân and ✓ Śân are svariteta. These roots are always found with सन् added to them. Without सन् we never find them conjugated either in the Âtmanepada or the Parasmaipada. When they have different meanings from those given to them in the above vârttikas, namely when they have the Dhâtupâṭha meaning of &c. they are considered to have no indicatory letters attached to them, and then they belong to the Churâdi class. Thus ✓ Gup to speak is Churâdi No. 231; ✓ Tij 'to sharpen' No. 110, ✓ Mâna 'to honor' No. 299, ✓ Badh 'to bind' No. 14. The Âtmanepada affixes are added to the roots ending in सन्, because in the case of these roots having the indicatory letter anudâtta as final there is no scope for the Âtmanepada affixes. For the simple roots Gup &c. are never found conjugated as such, and so the Anudâtta indicatory in Gup &c. does not mean, as it does everywhere else, that the simple roots ✓ Gupa &c. should be conjugated in the Âtmanepada; but that the san-added root ✓ Gup is to be so conjugated.

The affix सन् here is not an Ârdhadhâtuka affix, as it is in the regular Desideratives because this सन् is not ordained to be added to roots; but to specific terms 'gup' 'tij' &c. It is only where सन् is added by force of the sûtra धातोः (III. 1. 7. S. 2608) that it is Ârdhadhâtuka. The significant use of the word dhâtoḥ in III. 1. 7, while its absence from the two immediately preceding sûtras III. 1. 5 and 6, shows that the सन् of these two latter sûtras is not an Ârdhadhâtuka affix. Therefore it does not take the augment इट् nor does it cause Guņa.

As जुगुप्सते 'he censures or despises'; तितिक्षते 'he endures patiently'; चिकित्सति 'he heals'. But गोपायति 'he protects'; तेजयति 'he sharpens'; संकेतयति 'he makes sign'.

When सन् is added, there is reduplication of the root, by VI. 1. 9. Thus, गुप् + सन् = गुप् + स (VII. 4. 62) = जुगुप् + स to which is added the third person singular termination ते = जुगुप्सते ॥

The सन् is to be added only then, when the sense of the desiderative verb is as below: मीमांसते 'he investigates', बीभत्सते 'he loathes', दान्ते 'he straightens', शीशांसते 'he sharpens.' The verbs given in this and the preceding sûtra, are Desiderative in form, but not in meaning. The word 'optionally' in the next sûtra, may be read into this also, whereby the addition of सन् becomes optional. Thus मानयति, बाधयति, दानयति and निशानयति are also valid forms.

NOTE.—The ✓ Gup 'to be agitated,' (Divâdi No. 123), and ✓ Gup 'to protect' (Bhvâdi 422), are not to be taken for the purposes of this sûtra, because Gup here is read along with ✓ Tij, and therefore it refers to that ✓ Gup of the Dhâtupâṭha which is followed by Tij; and which is anudâtteta. In fact the anubandhas in ✓ Gupa, ✓ Tija, &c. is specially added to these roots in order to make them take âtmanepada affixes. For the letter अ being anudâtta, makes these ✓ Gup &c âtmanepadi. Though ✓ Gup &c are not full roots, but root elements, for the full root is gup + san, yet the âtmanepada ordained for the element applies to the root also, on the maxim अवयवे कृतं लिङ्गं समुदायस्य विशेषकं भवति (See Kâśikâ I. 3. 62). For if a mark (such as the anudâtta अ in ✓ Gupa) finds no scope in the part, it qualifies the whole because scope must be given to it. Therefore though the simple root-element ✓ Gupa cannot be conjugated in the Âtmanepada, the full root ✓ Jugupsa is Âtmanepadî by virtue of the indicatory anudâtta anubandha अ of ✓ Gup.

entries.english:
2396. The nasal of दंश, सञ्ज and स्वञ्ज, is elided before the vikaraṇa शप् of the roots of the Bhû class;

Note:—Thus दशति, सजति and परिष्वजते for the change of the स of स्वञ्ज to ष VIII. 3. 68.

2397. The nasal of रञ्ज् is also elided before शप् ॥

Note:—As रजति, रजतः, रजन्ति । The separation of this from the preceding is for the sake of the subsequent sûtras in which the anuvṛitti of ranj only runs and not of dañś &c.

Thus स्वजते । परिष्वजते । In another grammar we find the following

Rule. The roots ग्रन्थ, दम्भ, बन्ध and स्वञ्ज are optionally कित् when the affix of the Perfect follows.

[Note:—See I. 2. 6 in Kâśikâ, where however वा or 'optionally' is omitted.]

Thus देभतुः । Moreover we find the example सस्वजे in the Mahâbhâshya. See VIII. 3. 118 S. 2361. Therefore we adopt the above rule here also, though it is the opinion of a particular school only.

The s is not changed to ष after the reduplicate in the case of परिषस्वजे owing to the following.

Vartika:—In the sûtra VIII. 3. 118 S. 2361 (सदेः परस्य लिटि) we must enumerate स्वञ्ज also, i.e., the prohibition of that sûtra applies to स्वञ्ज. Therefore there is no change after the reduplicate.

Also,

Thus परिषस्वजे where the लिट् is कित् and causes the elision of the nasals or परिषस्वञ्जे where the लिट् is not treated as कित्.

Similarly 2nd Person Singular of the Perfect is सस्वञ्जिषे or सस्वक्षिषे ॥

1st Future स्वङ्क्ता । 2nd Future स्वङ्क्ष्यते ।

Pot.: स्वजेत । Benedictive: स्वङ्क्षीष्ट । Aorist: प्रत्यष्वक्त ॥

Here स is changed to ष by VIII. 3. 65 S. 2276, read with VIII. 3. 65 S. 2270. The present स्कन्दति । Perfect 2nd P. entries.english:
2398. The ष is optionally substituted for the स of स्कन्द after the preposition वि, but not in the participles in क्त and क्तवतु ॥

This rule is confined to कर्तृ affixes only, because of the prohibition of the affix निष्ठा । Thus विष्कन्ता or विस्कन्ता, विष्कन्तुम् or विस्कन्तुम्, विष्कन्तव्यम् or विस्कन्तव्यम् ।

Why do we say 'but not in the Nishtha'? Observe विस्कन्नः ॥

The same is the case when the prefix is परि by the following sûtra.

2399. ष is optionally substituted for the स of स्कन्द after the preposition परि everywhere.

Thus परिष्कन्दति or परिस्कन्दति । परिष्कन्ता or परिस्कन्ता, परिष्कन्तुम् or परिस्कन्तुम्, परिष्कन्तव्यम् or परिस्कन्तव्यम् ॥

The word परि could well have been included in the last sûtra as विपरिभ्यां स्कन्देः &c. The very fact that it has not been so included, indicates that the prohibition of अनिष्ठायाम् does not apply to it. Thus परिष्कन्नः or परिस्कन्नः ॥

When स is changed to ष, then न is also changed to ण । It cannot be said that the change depends upon two words, viz, the preposition and the word that follows it and therefore it is बहिरङ्ग and consequently असिद्ध or non-effective in applying an अन्तरङ्ग rule by the change of न to ण । For we have already said that an operation depending upon a verbal root and a preposition is an अन्तरङ्ग operation.

Moreover we find in the Bhâshya, the following rule laid down:—

The root is first joined with its preposition and then conjugated and affixes joined to it. But in the opinion of those who hold that the root is conjugated first and then the preposition added to it, there will be no ण change, and we shall get the form परिस्कन्नः ॥

entries.english:
2400. छ is substituted for the final of इष्, गम् and यम् before a Present-character (शित्).

Note:— As इच्छति, गच्छति, यच्छति । The इष् with the indicatory उ is taken here, (Tud. 59), and not of Divādi (19) class or of Kryādi class (53). There we have इष्यति and इष्णाति respectively. Those who do not read the sūtra as ‹?› &c., but as ‹?› &c., read the anuvṛitti of the word अचि from VII. 3. 72 into this sūtra; so that the शित् is qualified by the word ‹?› i. e. a शित् affix which is merely a vowel, and has no consonant in it; (and not a शित् affix which begins with a vowel.) Therefore though ‹?› is a शित् affix beginning with a vowel, yet as it contains a consonant, the substitution does not take place, as ‹?› (III. 1. 83). The reading of the text according to Patañjali and Kātyāyana is ‹?› and hence the necessity of the above explanation. The reading इषु, though convenient, is not ārṣa.

As गमिष्यति, अगमिष्यत्, जिगमिषति ॥

2403. ष is substituted for the स of निस् before the verb तप् when the meaning is not that of 'repeatedly making red hot.'

The word आसेवन means doing a thing repeatedly and here it means making it red-hot repeatedly. Thus निष्ठपति सुवर्णम् = सकृद् अग्निं स्पर्शयति i.e., he puts the gold into fire only once.

Why do we say when not meaning repeatedly? Observe निस्तपति सुवर्णं सुवर्णकारः = पुनः पुनरग्निं स्पर्शयति ॥

NOTE:—In the sentences निष्ठप्तं रक्षः, निष्टप्ता अरातयः the change has taken place either as a Vedic irregularity or because the sense of repeatedness is not implied here.

2405. The augment अम् (am) comes after the ऋ of सृज् 'to create,' and दृश् 'to see,' when an affix beginning with a झल् letter (the Mute and the Sibilant) follows: provided that it has no indicatory क् ॥

Thus where there is इट् augment we have ससर्जिथ; but when there is no इट् augment, we have the अम् and thus get सस्रष्ठ (VII. 2. 63. S. 2269). 1st. Fut. स्रष्टा ; 2nd Fut. स्रक्ष्यति । Ben. सृज्यात् । As the root has an indicatory ऌ the aorist is formed optionally by अङ् (III. 1. 57). When there is अङ् the following sútra applies :—

Note:—Thus सृज् + तृन् = स् + अम् + ऋज् + तृ = स्रष्टृ । Nom. sing. स्रष्टा. So also स्रष्टुम्, स्रष्टव्यम्, द्रष्टा, द्रष्टुम्, द्रष्टव्यम् । This अम् augment prevents the guna substitute ordained by VII. 3. 86. But in अस्राक्षीत् and अद्राक्षीत् the Vṛiddhi takes place in the Aorist, after the augment अम् had taken effect.

Why do we say when beginning with a Mute or a Sibilant ? Observe सर्जनम्, दर्शनम् with यु । Why do we say not having an indicatory क् ? Observe सृष्टः, दृष्टः, before the affix क्त । The forms of the roots being exhibited in the sútra, the rule applies when affixes relating to verbs come after these, and not when other affixes relating to nouns follow. Thus रज्जुसृड्भ्याम्, देवदृग्भ्याम् । Here the words are used as nouns rather than verbs. For the maxim धातोः स्वरूपग्रहणे तत्प्रत्यये कार्यं विज्ञायते applies here.

1038. √Daṁśa to bite. The word daśana 'actions of the teeth' i. e. biting. The word दशन is derived from this root. The nasal is elided by VI. 4. 25. S. 1034. Others say, the nasal is elided as a nipātana or anomaly, because the word दशन is so exhibited here. They also refer to this because the particularising of the meaning is modern. In other words, they also mean that दशन has lost its nasal because such is the usage of the masters of language, for Pṛiṣodarādi only validates the usage of the śiṣṭas. But in the Dhātupāṭha sútra दंश दशने the meaning दशन given to दंश is not the work of any ancient author : for all Dhātupāṭha meanings are recent additions to the bare list of roots prepared by Pāṇini : so any form occurring in these meanings cannot ipso facto be a standard. Therefore those who say that दशन is valid by nipātana here must be presumed to mean that standard writers have used the word daśana, which has been repeated here by the person or persons who have added these meanings to the roots. There they also indirectly mean that the form is valid under the Pṛiṣodarādi class.

Thus दंश + शप् + ति = दश् + अ + ति (the nasal is elided by VI. 4. 25. S. 2396) = दशति । The 2nd Per. Singular of the Perfect is ददंशिथ or ददंथ । First Future दंष्टा । Second Future दंक्ष्यति । Benedictive दश्यात् । Aorist अदाङ्क्षीत् ॥

1042. Kita to live, 2. to heal, cure. When meaning to doubt, it is generally preceded by वि । Thus विचिकित्सा means doubt, see Amarakosha I. 5. 3. It is Parasmaipadi but some take it to be anudātteta and so conjugate it in the Ātmanepadi. 2408. There takes place vocalisation of the semivowel of the reduplicate (abhyasa) of both vachyadi (VI. 1. 15) and grahadi (VI. 1. 16) words, when the affixes of लिट् follow.
Thus इयाज । In forming the Dual and Plural, the following sutra applies.
Note:—Thus वच्—उवाच, उवचिथ, स्वप्—सुष्वाप, सुष्वपिथ, यज्—इयाज, इयजिथ, डुवप्—उवाप, उपथ । As regards ग्रहादि verbs; ग्रह—जग्राह, जग्रहिथ (there is no speciality in the case of this verb, as these forms would have been evolved without even this rule). ज्या—जिज्यौ, जिज्यिथ; व्ये—संविवाय, and संविवयिथ; व्यध्—विव्याध, विव्यधिथ; वश्—उवाश, उवशिथ; व्यच्—विव्याच, विव्यचिथ; व्रश्च्—वव्राश्च and वव्रश्चिथ ।
This vocalisation of the reduplicate is taught with regard to those affixes which are not कित् । With regard to कित् affixes, the Rule VI. 1. 15 will apply.
entries.note: Devanagari verb examples in the Note reconstructed from clear grammatical context of grahadi/vachyadi lists.

entries.english:
2409. The semivowels of the roots वच्, स्वप्, and यजादि verbs are vocalised when followed by an affix having an indicatory क् ।
Thus यज् + अतुस् (which is कित् by I. 2. 5) = इ यज् + अतुस् = ईजतुः ।
The reduplication takes place after vocalisation.
And as the rule of vocalisation is subsequent to that of reduplication in order, therefore by the maxim of परस्य I. 4. 2, vocalisation will take place first and then reduplication, according to the maxim पुनः प्रसङ्गविज्ञानात्सिद्धम् "occasionally the formation of a particular form is accounted for by the fact that a preceding rule is allowed to apply again, after it had previously been superseded by a subsequent rule."
Note:—The anuvritti of ड्याट् does not run into this sutra. The root वच् includes the वच परिभाषणे of the Adadi class (II. 54) and the वच् substitute of ब्रू (II. 4. 53). स्वप् is the root णिष्वप् शये of the Adadi class (II. 59). The यजादि verbs are the last nine roots of the Bhvadi class viz. यज्, वप्, वह्, वस्, वेञ्, व्येञ्, ह्वेञ्, वद् and श्वि ॥ The semivowels of these eleven verbs are changed into the corresponding vowels, when an affix having an indicatory क् is added to them. Thus with the Past Participle affixes क्त and क्तवतु we have the following forms:—1. वच्—उक्तः, उक्तवान् (VIII. 2. 30), 2. स्वप्—सुप्तः, सुप्तवान्, 3. यज्—इष्टः, इष्टवान् (VIII. 2. 36), 4. वप्—उप्तः, उप्तवान्, 5. वह्—ऊढः, ऊढवान् (VIII. 2. 31, 40, VIII. 3. 13 and VI. 3. 111), 6. वस्—उषितः, उषितवान् (VII. 2. 56, VIII. 3. 60), 7. वेञ्—उतः, उतवान्, 8. व्येञ्—संवीतः, संवीतवान्, 9. ह्वेञ्—हूतः, हूतवान्, 10. वद्—उदितः, उदितवान्, 11. ‹?›—शूनः, शूनवान् ॥

2410. The ष is substituted for the स of शास, वस, and घस, when it is preceded by an इण् vowel or a guttural.
Note:—Thus अन्वशिषत्, अन्वशिषताम्, अन्वशिषन्, the Aorist of शास; the च्लि is replaced by अङ् (III. 1. 56), and the आ changed to इ by VI. 4. 34. So also शिष्टः, शिष्टवान् ॥ From वच्, उक्तिः, उक्तवान्, उक्त्वा । The Samprasarana takes place by VI. 1. 15 as it belongs to Yajadi class. From घस्, we have अक्षतुः, in the Perfect. घस् is the substitute of अद् (II. 4. 37), the penultimate is elided by
entries.note: Entry text cut off at end of page 247.

VI. 4. 98. So also may in ‹?› (Rig. I. 82. 2). This is the Aorist form of अद्, the घस् is substituted for अद् (II. 4. 37): the Aorist sign is elided by II. 4. 80.

Thus ऊचतुः । Pl. ऊषुः । 2nd S. उवसिथ or उवस्थ । The First Future is वस्ता । The second Future is thus formed वस् + स्यति । Here the स of वस् is changed to त् by VII. 4. 49. S. 2313.

We have therefore, वत्स्यति । The Benedictive is उष्यात् । The aorist is अवात्सीत् । अवात्ताम् ॥

entries.english:
2411. When लिट् follows, वय is optionally the substitute of वेञ् 'to weave.'

The इ in वयि is for the sake of pronunciation only. The substitute is वय् । Thus वय् + णल् = वय् + वय् + अ (VI. 1. 8. S. 2177) = उय् + वय् + अ (VI. 1. 17. S. 2408) = उवाय । In the dual we have वय् + अतुस् = उय् + वय् + अतुस् ॥

The dual affix अतुस् being कित् (I. 2. 5) the following sútra would have applied and caused the vocalisation of य्; but it is not so by the sútra that follows, namely S. 2413.

2412. There is vocalisation of the semi-vowels of the following verbs, when an affix having an indicatory क् or ङ् follows: ग्रहि 'to take', ज्या 'to become old', वयि 'to weave', व्यधि 'to strike', वष्टि 'to shine', व्यच 'to deceive', व्रश्च 'to cut', प्रच्छ 'to ask', and भृज्ज 'to cook, to fry.'

The य required vocalisation, which is however prevented by

2413. In the substituted root वय (II. 4. 41), the य in the Perfect is not vocalised.

The phrase संप्रसारणं is understood here. Thus उवाय, ऊयतुः, ऊयुः । The word लिट् is employed in this aphorism for the sake of subsequent sutras, this one could have done well without it even.

Though the य is not vocalised, it is optionally replaced by व by the following sútra.

2414. Before the tense affixes of the Perfect that have an indicatory क् (I. 2. 5), for the य् of वय् may optionally be substituted व् ॥

Thus ऊयतुः or ऊवतुः, ऊयुः or ऊवुः ॥

NOTE:—According to Patanjali, the phrase वश्चास्य of this sútra could have been dispensed with; this much would have been enough:—अन्यतरस्यां किति वेञः ।

Thus वे + अतुस् = व + व + अतुस् = ववतुः and ववुः (the vocalisation being prohibited).

In the alternative: वा + अतुस् = उ + अतुस् = उ + उवङ् + अतुस् (VI. 1. 77) = ऊवतुः, ऊवुः ॥ Here there is vocalisation. In the case of a substitute, the य is never vocalised, so we have ऊयतुः, ऊयुः । Thus all the three forms have been evolved without using वश्चास्य ॥

In the 2nd S. there is always इट् augment, in spite of VII. 2. 62. S. 2295, because वय is defective and can never be conjugated in the First Future with तास् । Thus we have उवयिथ ॥

The defective root वय being the substitute of वेञ् is considered to have an indicatory ञ, by I. 1. 56. S. 49 and so is conjugated in the Parasmai and Atmane both. Thus Atmane—Perfect is ऊये or ऊवे ॥

When there is no वय substitution for वे in the Perfect, the following sútra applies.

2415. The semivowel of वे 'to weave' is not vocalised in the Perfect.

Thus ववौ, ववतुः, ववुः । This root belongs to यजादि class and would have been vocalised before कित् affixes by VI. 1. 15; and before non-कित् affixes the Reduplicate syllable of the Perfect would have been vocalised by VI. 1. 17. Both vocalisations are prohibited here.

1055. Veñ to weave. व्येञ् १०५६ संवरणे । व्ययति ॥

1056. Vyeñ to cover.
The Present is व्ययति । In the Perfect, the sútra VI. 1. 45. S. 2370 required the to be changed into आ; but the following sútra prevents that.

entries.english:
2416. There is not the substitution of आ for the Diphthong of the root व्ये when the affixes of the Perfect follow.

Thus संविव्याय, संविव्ययिथ । The reduplicate of the Perfect is vocalised here by VI. 1. 17. The Vriddhi in संविव्याय takes place by VII. 2. 115 before the णल् affix ॥

Though in the reduplicate, the य् required to be elided by VII. 4. 60. S. 2179 because it is subsequent to the rule of samprasárana; yet the latter prevails and the य is vocalised to इ (Had VII. 4. 60. S. 2179 applied then the vocalisation would have been of व् ।) This we do, because of the word ubhayeshám being used in the sútra VI. 1. 17. S. 2408. For there was no necessity of using this word in the sútra VI. 1. 17, S. 2408, as the anuvritti of Vachyádi and yajádi was already current in it.

Though the phrase उभयेषाम् could have been supplied into this sútra by the context and the governing scope of the preceding sútras, its express mention in this sútra is for the sake of indicating, that the rule of vocalisation supersedes even the rule of हलादिः शेषः VII. 4. 60, the vocalisation must take place at all events. Thus व्ये + णल् = व्ये + व्ये + अ Here by VII. 4. 60, the second consonant य of व्ये ought to have been elided, and the equation would have stood वे + व्ये + अ and there would have been vocalisation of व् by VI. 1. 17. S. 2408. But that is not intended. There is vocalisation of य and we have विव्याय । In fact the universal maxim of vocalisation is: "The samprasárana and the operation dependent on it possess greater force than other operations which are simultaneously applicable."

1057. Hveñ. To emulate, to call by name.
The following sútra applies in forming its Perfect.

2417. There is vocalisation of the semivowel of ह्वे in the reduplicated form, in both the syllables.

NOTE:—The abhyasta means the reduplicate and the reduplicated, both the syllables. The vocalisation takes place before reduplication. Thus जुहाव, जुहुवतुः,

and वति । This and the last sutra are one, in the original of Panini, they have been divided into two by the authority of a Vârtika.
The root is vocalised first and then reduplicated. In other words, when such an affix follows which will cause reduplication, then becomes by vocalisation, first, and it is reduplicated afterwards. For the purposes of reduplication ‹?› is the proper stem. Thus जुहाव । Dual जुहुवतुः, (VI. 4. 77 S. 271) Pl. जुहुवुः । 2nd S. जुहोथ or जुहविथ Atm. 3. 2418. After the verbs लिप् 'to paint,' सिच् 'to sprinkle' and ह्वे 'to call,' अङ् is the substitute of च्लि when लुङ् follows signifying the agent.
Note:—Thus अलिपत् 'he painted or wrote'; असिचत् 'he sprinkled'; and अह्वत् 'he called or challenged.'
But there is option in the Atmanepada.

2419. After the verbs लिप्, सिच् and ह्वे, अङ् is optionally the substitute of च्लि, when the affixes of the Atmanepada follow.
Thus (अलिपत or अलिप्त 'he painted'; असिचत or असिक्त 'he sprinkled';) अह्वत or अह्वात 'he challenged.' There is elision of आ by VI. 4. 64. S. 2372.

The Present is श्वि+शप्+तिप्=श्वयति । In the Perfect there is vocalisation optionally by the following.

entries.english:
2420. There is optionally the vocalisation of the semivowel of श्वि before the affixes of the Perfect and the Intensive.
The phrases लिटि यङोः and सम्प्रसारणम् are to be read into this sútra. Thus शुशाव । श्वि + अ = ( शु + अ VI. 1. 30) = शु + आव् (VI. 1. 108) = शु + शु + अ (VI. 1. 8) = शुशाव । (with vriddhi). Or शिश्वाय, शुशुवतुः or शिश्वियतुः । So also in the Intensive as शीशूयते or शेश्वीयते । The root श्वि would not have taken vocalisation before यङ् by any previous rule, this sútra teaches optional vocalisation. The root would have taken vocalisation before लिट्, which is a कित् affix, invariably by VI. 1. 15, this sútra modifies that by making the substitution optional.
Vârtika:—In the alternative, when the reduplicate is also not vocalised in spite of VI. 1. 17. This explains the form शिश्वाय, which by VI. 1. 17 would have been शुश्वाय ॥
The aorist is optionally formed by अङ् (III. 1. 58. S. 2291). When the aorist is formed by अङ्, the following sutra applies.
entries.note: Embedded Devanagari and minor OCR errors corrected.

2421. The अ is substituted for the final of श्वि in the अङ् Aorist.
As अश्वत्, अश्वताम्, अश्वन् । For the अ of the stem and the अ of the affix there is the single substitute of the last by VI. 1. 97. See III. 1. 58.
Optionally the Aorist is formed by reduplication (चङ्) by III. 1. 49. S. 2375. Thus अशिश्वियत् । Here there is इयङ् substitution by VI. 4. 77. S. 271, as it is antaranga and therefore stronger than guna.
When the ordinary aorist is formed with सिच्, then by VII. 2. 5. S. 2299 there is no Vriddhi and we get the form अश्वयीत् ॥
Here end the yajadi roots.
The Bhvadi class is an Akritigana. All roots not otherwise classified, fall under this class. As चुलुम्पति &c.

Before we take up the conjugation of the regular roots commencing with अद् 'to eat'; we shall show the conjugation of the sautra root ऋती, which is treated like the roots of this class.
2422. The affix ईयङ् comes after the sutra root ऋति 'to reproach' without changing the sense.
Note:—The indicatory ङ् shows that the verb will take the affixes of the Atmanepada; as ऋतीयते 'he pities or reproaches'; so also, ऋतीयाते, ऋतीयन्ते ॥
Many say that the meaning of this root is 'to reproach.' But others say it means 'to pity.' The whole form ऋतीय gets the designation of dhatu and is called 'root,' by S. 2304.
Thus the Present is ऋतीयते, the Perfect is ऋतीयां चक्रे ॥
The addition of ईयङ् is optional when the affix of the Ardhadhatuka follows (S. 2305). So when the ईयङ् is not added, the root is Parasmaipadi by the universal sutra 2159. Thus another form of the Perfect is आनर्त ॥
The Future is अर्तिष्यति । The Aorist is आर्त्तीत् ॥
Pre. ऋतीयते । Per. ऋतीयांचक्रे or आनर्त । I Fut. ऋतीयिता । अर्तिता । II Fut. ऋतीयिष्यति । अर्तिष्यति । Aorist. आर्तीयिष्ट । आर्त्तीत् ॥
अद् भक्षणे । द्वौ परस्मैपदिनौ ॥

The Adadi verbs belong to the second conjugation. In this class of verbs, therefore, the terminations are added direct to the root.

entries.english:
2428. The final nasal of those roots which in the Dhâtupâṭha have an unaccented root-vowel, as well as of वन and तन &c., is elided before an affix beginning with a consonant (except a semi-vowel or nasal), when these have an indicatory क् or ङ् ॥

Note:— Thus यम् gives us यत्वा (with क्त्वा), यतः (with क्त), यतवान् (with क्तवतु), यतिः (with क्तिन्). Similarly रम् gives us रत्वा, रतः, रतवान्, रतिः । यम्, रम्, नम्, गम्, हन् and मन् which end in a nasal are to be considered as unaccented roots, though taught as accented in the Dhâtupâṭha. So also of खन् i. e., खतिः with क्तिन्. With क्तिच् the nasal is not elided as खन्तिः (VI. 4. 39); and before other jhalâdi affixes खन् retains न् as all those affixes take the augment इट् ।

The तनादि roots belong to the eighth class. Thus ततः, ततवान् ।

The Tanâdi roots are ten in number, तन्, षण्, क्षण्, क्षिण्, ऋण्, तृण्, घृण्, वन, मन् and कृण् । Of these षण् takes long आ also (VI. 4. 45) षा....षातः, षातवान्; क्षा....क्षातः, क्षातवान्; तृण्....तातः, तृतवान्; घृण्....घातः, घातवान्; वन....वातः, वातवान्; मन्....मातः, मातवान् ॥

The word अनुनासिक is in the genitive case the sign of the genitive being suppressed. This qualifies all but one word वनोति of the sûtra. The roots Yam, Ram, Nam, Gam, Han and Man are taught as Anudâtta. The Tanâdi roots are Tan, Kshan, Kshin, Rin, Trin, Ghrin, Van, and Man. Thus हन् + तः = ह् + तः = हतः ॥

The Third Person Plural is formed thus:— हन् + अन्ति = ह् + अन्ति (VI. 4. 98 S. 2363) = घ् + अन्ति (VII. 3. 54. S. 358) = घ्नन्ति ॥

When an alterant upasarga is added, the न is changed to ण by the following Sûtra.

entries.english:
2429. Optionally when व or म follows, the न of √han is changed to ण, when preceded by an upasarga competent to cause change.

Thus प्रहण्वः, परिहण्वः, or प्रहन्वः and परिहन्वः, प्रहण्मः or प्रहन्मः, परिहण्मः or परिहन्मः ।

This sûtra enjoins an option in certain cases, where it would have been obligatory by the last Ashtadhyayi rule VIII. 4. 22.

In forming the perfect, the ह is changed to a guttural by VII. 3. 54 S. 358.

PRESENT.
Sing. Dual. Plural.
Third Person, हन्ति । हतः । घ्नन्ति ।
Second Person, हंसि । हथः । हथ ।
First Person, हन्मि । हन्वः । हन्मः ।

Now we take up लिट् or the Perfect.

हन् + णल् = हन् हन् + अ = जहन् + अ = जघन् + अ by VII. 3. 54, S. 358 = जघान । The dual is जघ्नतुः and the Plural is जघ्नुः ॥

In forming the 2nd Pers. Singular, the following sûtra applies:—

2430. A Guttural is substituted for the ह in हन् after a reduplication also.

Note:— As जिघांसति, जङ्घन्यते, प्रघानः ॥ The rule applies when such an affix follows which causes the reduplication of the stem (aṅga) हन्, therefore not in ‹?›—‹?› ॥

Thus we get जघनिथ or जघन्थ ।

Note:— Although this sûtra could apply to the third person singular as well, yet VII. 3. 54 alone has been mentioned simply because it is antaraṅga.

Second Person. जघनिथ or जघन्थ । जघ्नथुः । जघ्न ।

In forming the Imperative 2nd Per. Sing. the following applies:—

2431. ज is substituted for हन् before हि ॥

Thus जहि 'kill thou.'

This ज substitute of हन् is ordained by VI. 4. 36, a rule belonging to the Âbhîya section (asiddhavad atrabhât VI. 4. 22 S. 2193); therefore it is considered asiddha or not to have taken effect for the purposes of the elision of हि. For had ज been considered as valid, then हि would have been elided by VI. 4. 105 S. 2202.

Thus the Conjugation of हन् in the Imperative is:—

In conjugating हन् in लङ्, the Third Person Sing is thus formed अ + हन् + ति = अ + हन् + त् = अहन् the letter त् being elided by VI. 1. 68.

Thus we conjugate the root:—

In the Benedictive वध replaces हन् by the following sûtras.
2432. The clause 'when the affix is ârdhadhâtuka' is understood in the following aphorisms up to the aphorism 58 of the fourth chapter of the second Book of Panini.
2433. वध is the substitute of हन् 'to kill' when the ârdhadhâtuka लिङ् (Benedictive) follows.

2434. And when लुङ् (Aorist) follows वध is the substitute of हन् ॥

The substitute is vadha ending with an अ. Thus वध्यात् 'may he kill,' वध्यास्ताम् 'may they two kill,' वध्युः 'may they all kill.'

As the substitute वध ends in short अ, this अ is elided by S. 2308 because vadha ends in an अ, at the time when the ârdhadhâtuka affix is taught. This elision being like the original (Sthânivat I. 1. 56), in forming the Aorist
entries.note: Text cuts off at end of page 259.

entries.english: [have] अवध + ‹?› = अवधीत् । Here zero being sthānivat prevents the vṛiddhi of ‹?› which otherwise would have taken place by VII. 2. 7. Note:—अवधीत् 'he killed,' अवधीष्टाम् 'they all killed.' The division of this aphorism from the last sūtra (yoga-vibhāga) indicates that the next Ashtadhyayi rule II. 4. 44 applies to the Aorist only and not to the Benedictive as well. There is no option in the Benedictive Ātmanepada. The word चार्धधातुके in S. 2432 is in the 7th case; the force of this case affix here is not that given in I. 1. 66. i. e. the sūtra does not mean 'when an ārdhadhātuka affix follows.' But the 7th case has the force of indicating the subject (विषय) the meaning of the sūtra being 'when the subject is an Ārdhadhātuka affix.' The result of this explanation is, that the various substitutions enjoined hereafter, should be made first, and then the respective affixes should be applied. Thus whenever we want to affix any Ārdhadhātuka-affix to अस 'to be,' we must first substitute भू for it, and then take the proper ārdhadhātuka affix which would come with regard to भू. Thus we can apply यत् to भू by rule III. 1. 97. which says 'after verbs ending in vowels यत् is applied.' But this affix could never have been applied to अस, which ends in a consonant. Thus we have भव्यम्. So the substitution does not depend upon any particular affix, but ārdhadhātuka affixes as a class. Or to take the example of वध । This vadha ends with अ and is the substitute of हन् which ends with a consonant. But to वध will be applied all those rules which can apply to a root ending with a vowel, when an ārdhadhātuka affix is to be added. Thus अतो लोपः of 2308 will apply to this final अ of वध and cause its elision. Thus वध्यात्, वध्यास्ताम् । Why do we say 'when an ārdhadhātuka affix is to be added'? चक्षिङ् व्यक्तायां वाचि ।

Chakshin व्यक्तायां वाचि । 'to speak articulately.' This root also means to see, as विश्वा संपाभिचष्टे शचीभिः । The letter ङ in चक्षिङ् is indicatory of the fact that the affix युच् is added to the root by III. 2. 149 S. 3129; which would not have been the case had the root not contained this anudâtta ङ. Thus विचक्षणः ‹?›.

This ङ though indicatory, does not cause the insertion of the nasal नुम् because we have explained the word इदितः by पदस्य इदितः in the sûtra VII. 1. 58. S. 2262 because the word पदस्य is understood here from the preceding Ashtadhyayi sûtra 'noh padânte' VII. 1. 57. S. 3574. So that only those roots are 'इदित्' for the purposes of नुम् augment, which contain the इ as their final. The इ in चक्षिङ् is not final and so the root is not इदित् for the purposes of that sûtra.

What is the use of the letter ङ when the root is already ubhayapadî?

Ans. The ङ indicates by implication the existence of the following maxim:—

The âtmanepada which is caused by an anudâtteta letter, is anitya. Thus the Present Participle form स्फायन् is valid; as in the example स्फायन्निर्मोकसन्धिः &c. Here स्फीय् is used as parasmaipadî though ordinarily it is Âtmanepadî because the root स्फायी has anudâtta long ई as indicatory. See Bhvâdi No I. 516.

Thus we have (the स् is elided by VIII. 2. 29. S. 380) चष्टे &c.

In forming the Perfect, the following two sûtras apply: which are governed by the anuvritti of Ârdhadhâtuka of the rule 2377.

entries.english: 2436. ख्याञ् is the substitute of चक्षिङ् 'to perceive, to tell,' when any Ârdhadhâtuka affix is to be applied.

2437. ख्या is optionally the substitute of चक्षिङ् when लिट् (Perfect) follows.

In the Mahâbhâshya the substitute begins with क and is क्शा. The श is changed to ख optionally by the vârtika ख्यो वा । This vârtika reads in the section of asiddhas. As the substitute has an indicatory ङ it is conjugated in both padas. — Thus the perfect is चख्यौ or चख्ये । or चख्यतुः or चख्याते ॥

Note:—In the Mahâbhâshya on II. 4. 54 S. 2436 we find Patanjali saying that the substitute begins with क and is क्शां — This substitute Khśâṅ assumes the form Khyâṅ also. Thus by substituting य for श under the following vârtika:—शिर्योर्या वा विधीयते 'The letter य optionally replaces the श of this substitute; and this is asiddha, because this vârtika ought to be put in the section of asiddhas (VIII. 2. 1.) just at the close of the rules relating to the change of छ to श.' That being so, for the application of the prior rules the य is considered asiddha, but for the application of the subsequent rule, it is considered siddha. Thus, here श changed to य is asiddha and so the sûtra कुहोश्चुः does not apply and क is not changed to च.

Note:—Prohibition must be stated when चक्षिङ् means 'exclusion'; as अपचक्षाः कुशलाः 'bad men should be excluded.'

Note:—Prohibition must be stated when the affixes घञ् and ण्वुल् follow; as विचक्षणः, प्रख्यानशीलः 'the Rakshasas are cruel.' This is Vedic Sanskrit; modern राक्षसाः क्रूराः. The meaning of the root here, is 'to injure.' So also चक्षुषः प्रसिद्धत्वम्; here the affix is उसि.

The substitute क्शा becomes क्शा by VIII. 4. 55. S. 121. This is conjugated as चक्शे । A. चक्शे ।

The vârtika शस्य खत्वे विप्रतिषेधात् (See S. 130 and 294) required क्शा to be changed to ख्शा; giving the form चख्शे, but that vârtika also does not apply because rule VIII. 4. 55. S. 121 by which the root was changed to क्शा is considered asiddha, so that for the purposes of that vârtika, the root is still चक्ष् ॥

From the root चक्ष् itself, we get the perfect regularly. Thus चचक्षे । The First Future is ख्याता or चक्षाता । The Second Future is ख्यास्यति or ख्यास्यते । Or क्शास्यति or क्शास्यते ॥ The Imperfect is अचष्ट । The Potential is चक्षीत । The Benedictive is ख्यायात् or क्शायात् or क्शेयात् ।

2438. After the verbs अस् 'to throw', वच् 'to speak', and ख्या 'to speak', अङ् is the substitute of च्लि, when the Aorist follows signifying the agent.

NOTE:—ख्या may be either the root, or the substitute of चक्ष् (II. 4. 54) and so also वच् may be the root, or the substitute of ब्रू (II. 4. 53). The root अस् belonging to the दिवादि or the Fourth conjugation, falls under the subdivision पुषादि, and therefore it would have taken अङ् in the Parasmaipada by rule III. 1. 55. The repetition is to indicate that it takes अङ् in the Âtmanepada also; as अध्यस्थत (VII. 4. 17), आस्थात् and अस्थत्. In the Passive, we have आस्थिषाताम् —

Thus the aorist is P. अख्यत् or A. अख्यत or अख्याताम् or अख्यन्त इत्यादि ॥

Ishti:—The substitute does not take place when the meaning is 'exclusion', as अपचष्टे &c.

Note:—The following from Mâdhavîya Dhâtuvritti will make this clear.

In the Mahâbhâshya the author has given the two substitutes 'ख्याञ् and क्शाञ्' first, and then he, in the alternative, gives one substitute which includes both ख्या and क्शा, for it can assume both these forms. For क्शा becomes ख्या by the rule (VIII. 4. 55. S. 121). And ख्या also becomes क्शा by the operation of a vârtika which changes the ‹?› into ‹?›, and this is considered asiddha when a prior rule is to be applied, because that Vârtika is read in the section of asiddhas, just after the change rules.

The necessity of taking the substitute to be ‹?› will be manifest from the following considerations:—

(a) In forming an abstract noun from ‹?›, such as ‹?›. This is formed by ‹?› affix V. 1. 124. S. 1788. But if ‹?› be considered to have a penultimate ‹?› (as in fact it has, but which under the above rule we consider as ‹?›) then the affix would have been ‹?› by V. 1. 132. S. 1797; and the form ought to have been ‹?›. But we never have this form: because V. 1. 132. S. 1797 does not apply, as the existence of ‹?› in ‹?› is ignored by it and to it, it is ‹?›. This is summed up in the vârtika: ‹?›.

(b) Similarly पुंसः ख्यानं पुंख्यानं । Here the स् of पुंस् being elided as the final of a conjunct consonant (VIII. 2. 23. S. 54); we have पुं + ख्यानम् । Now by the vârtika under S. 139, the म् of पुम् would be changed to ‹?›, because ख्यान begins with ख, a letter of खर् pratyâhâra, and is followed by य, a letter of यण् pratyâhâra, and so S. 139 ought to apply. The form ought to be ‹?›. But this is not so, because the य in ख्या is considered asiddha and so ख is not followed by a letter of यण् pratyâhâra; and so the condition for the application of S. 139 does not exist. This is summed up by the vârtika ‹?›.

(c) Similarly विध्ये । We get this form thus: विख्या + ल् + ध्वे = वि + ख् + य + ध्वे । Here ख्, a letter of झष् pratyâhâra is followed by ध, and therefore VIII. 3. 78 S. 2325 requires the ध to be changed to ढ. But this is not done, because य is asiddha, and so there is no letter of झष् pratyâhâra in विध्ये and so VIII. 3. 78 S. 2325 does not apply.

(d) Similarly चक्षुःख्यातः । Here the visarga is followed by a letter of शर् pratyâhâra; and the शर् itself is followed by ‹?› (for ख is ‹?›), a letter of खर् pratyâhâra, and so VIII. 3. 35. S. 150 applies, and the visarga remains unchanged. But, if the substitute were not ‹?›, then being followed by ख would have brought in the application of VIII. 3. 37 S. 142, and the visarga would be changed to jihvâmûlîya. But this is not so. This is summed up in the vârtika:—संस्थानप्रतिषेधः । Samsthâna means the jihvâmûlîya change.

(e) Similarly the Nishthâ is with न. Had the य been really य and not श in disguise, then the root would be a yan-anta or semi-vowel having root, and VIII. 2. 43. S. 3017 would apply, and त would be changed to न. This is

(f) Similarly पर्याख्यानम् । Here न is not changed to ण, though between the र of पर्या and न, there are only अट् pratyāhāra letters य्, आ, ख्, या, and letter आ; and so the Sūtra VIII. 4. 2, S. 197 read with VIII. 4. 29, S. 2835 would have applied. entries.english:
2439. The sarvadhatuka affix से (the ending of the second Person Present and Imperative Atmanepada) gets the augment इट् after ईड् (Ad. 9).

Note:— As ईडिषे and ईडिष्वे ॥ से becomes स्व by III. 4. 91 and 80. The से is exhibited in the sutra without any case ending.

2440. The sarvadhatuka affix से and ध्वे, (the endings of the Present and the Imperative Atmanepadi) get the augment इट् after the roots ईड् (Ad. 9) and जन् ॥

Note:— Thus ईडिध्वे, ईडिध्वम्, ईडिषे, ईडिष्व, जनिध्वे, जनिध्वम्, जनिषे, जनिष्व । The root जनी (IV. 41) is taken here. The Vikarana श्यन् has been elided in this case, as a Vedic irregularity, and so also there is not elision of the penultimate अ. This sūtra could well have been included in the last. The making of it a separate sūtra is a mere amplification and a variety. Thus ईड् + ध्वे = ईड् + इ + ध्वे ॥ The affix इट् will come before the स्व of the Imperative also; for though स्व is not strictly speaking से and these rules do not strictly apply to स्व, yet they would apply on the maxim "a form modified in a portion of it is not different from the original." So से and स्व, ध्वे and ध्वम् are one and the same, as ईडिषे and ईडिष्व ॥ By using the word विकृत in the above vārtika, the original affix ध्वम् (prakriti) is not to be taken. Therefore we have अकृध्वम् in कृ where no augment is added, in other words when ध्वे is changed to ध्वम् by III. 4. 91, S. 2253 this ध्वम् is vikriti or a modified form of ध्वे, and a rule applicable to ध्वे will apply to this ध्वम् ॥ But when ध्वम् is not a modified form of ध्वे but an original affix (prakriti) the rule applicable to ध्वे will not apply to it. 2441. For the vowel of शीङ् there is substituted guṇa, when a Sārvadhātuka affix follows.

Note:—But शिश्ये before the ārdhadhātuka affix (III. 4. 115). Though these sārvadhātuka affixes were ङित् (I. 2. 4. S. 2234) and would not have caused guṇa (I. 1. 5. S. 2217), they do so by virtue of the present sûtra. The word शीङ् is read in the sûtra with the anubandha, in order to indicate that the rule does not apply to yaṅ-luk as शेशीते, शेश्यते । In forming the plural the following rule applies.

2442. The अत् substitute of झ gets the augment रुट्, after the root शीङ्.

Thus शेरते, शेरताम्, अशेरत ॥

Note:—The augment रुट् is added at the beginning of the affix, making it रत्. Had this been an augment of झ, then like the आट् augment in शयाताम्, it would have intervened between the शी and झ, and not immediately following a non-stem, would not have been substituted for झ at all. Therefore रुट् is made the augment of the substitute अत्, and not of झ ॥

The root is read in the sûtra with its anubandha in order to indicate, that there is no augment when there is elision of the Intensive affix yaṅ, nor any Guṇa. As शेश्यते, अशेश्यत ॥

entries.english:
2446. The letters n, d, or r, when preceded by a vowel, and forming the first letter of a conjunct consonant, are not reduplicated.
Note:—The word dvitiyasya "of the second syllable," is understood here. This sutra debars the doubling of the consonants n, d, and r when forming parts of the second syllable, provided these letters occur in the beginning of a conjunct (sanyoga) letter. Thus the Desiderative root of ‹?› is ‹?›, formed by adding सन् and ‹?›. The second syllable here is ‹?›, which is to be reduplicated by the last rule. But in doing so, ‹?› will not be doubled. Thus we get the form ‹?›; so also from ‹?› and ‹?›, we have ‹?›, and ‹?›.
Note:—Why do we say "when ‹?› and ‹?› are the letters"? Observe ‹?› from ‹?› in which ‹?› is the initial letter and has been reduplicated into ‹?›. Why do we say "being the first letter in a conjunct consonant"? Observe प्राणिणिषति from the root अन् 'to breathe', the n being changed into ṇ by VIII. 4. 19 and 21. The phrase ‹?› of the last sûtra is understood in this sutra also. Thus ‹?›. Some explain the word ‹?› understood in this sûtra in the same way as in the last, namely as a karmadharaya compound in the Ablative singular. They do so, in order to explain the form ‹?›, which is thus evolved: ‹?› इन्द्र + क्यच् III. 1. 8 = इन्द्रीय ॥ Then ‹?›. Here though the second syllable consists of n, d and r, yet न alone is rejected in reduplication and not द and र also, as द and र are not immediately after the initial vowel (अचि) in this case.
Therefore in ‹?› the syllable ‹?› will be reduplicated and not the ‹?› of ‹?›. Thus ‹?›. Here the syllable ‹?› is considered as ‹?› for the purposes of doubling; because the ‹?› in ‹?› was obtained by changing ‹?› into ‹?› by applying the Tripadī sûtra VIII. 4. 1. S. 235. and such a change is asiddha for the application of Sapāda rules. (See VIII. 2. 1 S. 12). Thus we get ‹?›.
Q. What of the maxim which says that in the case of reduplication the Sūtra VIII. 2. 1. S. 12, does not hold good: and which therefore required that ‹?› should be reduplicated into ‹?›?
Ans. To this we answer that the maxim quoted by you (पूर्वत्रासिद्धीयमद्विर्वचने) is not of universal application. This we infer from the implication of VIII. 4. 21. S. 2606. That sûtra says "Both the n's are changed into ṇ in the reduplicated forms of the root, when preceded by an alterant preposition". Thus the root ‹?›. The Desiderative root from it is ‹?›. If the maxim above given were of universal application then the reduplicated form would be ‹?› and there would have been no necessity of the sutra. The very fact that sutra requires both to be changed to ‹?› shows the limited scope of this maxim. The following note on VIII. 4. 21. S. 2606 will explain the point better:—
Note.—If the maxim पूर्वत्रासिद्धीयमद्विर्वचने be not applied here; then we have the following dilemma in, ‹?›. Here the affix ‹?› requires reduplication, and the present sûtra requires change of n. The ‹?› being asiddha, the reduplication being made first, we have ‹?›, and then the reduplicate intervenes between the cause and root-n of ‹?›, and so this n would not be changed to ‹?›. If however the above maxim be applied, we first apply the rule as ‹?›, and then reduplicate ‹?›; and we get the form ‹?› even without this sutra.
Note.—If we could get this form by the application of the above maxim where is the necessity of the present sûtra? The sûtra is necessary in order to indicate that the above maxim is anitya or not of universal application. And because it is anitya, that the form ऊर्णुनाव is evolved by reduplicating णु (See VIII. 2. 1).
Therefore णु in the reduplicate here becomes नु and we get ऊर्णुनाव by vṛiddhi. Dual ऊर्णुनुवतुः । Plural ऊर्णुनुवुः । In forming 2nd Person singular the following sutra applies.

entries.english:
2447. After the verb ūrṇu 'to cover,' the affix beginning with the augment इट् is regarded optionally like ङित्.
Thus before the थल् termination of the 2nd Per. we may have either ऊर्णुनुविथ or ऊर्णोनविथ । The 1st Future is ऊर्णुविता or ऊर्णविता । The equation of the form is: ऊर्णु + इट् + ता = ऊर्णुव् + इ + ता (VI. 4. 77) = ऊर्णुविता । When the affix is not regarded as ङित्, it produces guṇa, and we have the second form ऊर्णविता ।
Note:—Of course there is no option allowed before those affixes which do not take the augment इट् and before those terminations, consequently, we have only one form: as प्रोर्णु + ल्युट् = प्रोर्णो + अनम् = प्रोर्णवनम् 'covering,' प्रोर्णवनीयम् 'which ought to be covered.'

entries.english:
2448. Before a पित् Sārvadhātuka affix which is a single consonant, Guṇa is substituted for the final of ऊर्णु ॥
This debars Vṛiddhi. As और्णोत्, और्णोः ॥ Though the anuvṛitti of हलि was understood in this sûtra from the last aphorism VII. 3. 90, the employment of the term अपृक्ते implies the existence of the following maxim:—यस्मिन्विधिस्तदादावल्ग्रहणे "when a term which denotes a letter is exhibited in a rule, in the form of a Locative case, and qualifies something else which likewise stands in the Locative case, that which is qualified by it must be regarded as beginning with the letter which is denoted by the term in question, and not as ending with it".
In the Potential we have ऊर्णुयात्, ऊर्णुयाः etc. Here there is no Vṛiddhi even in the 3rd singular numbers. For though तिप्, सिप्, मिप् are पित् and so also their substitutes; and though they ought to cause Vṛiddhi by VII. 3. 89. S. 2443, yet as we have already said before, according to the Bhāṣhya an affix which is specifically called ङित् loses its general character of पित्; and vice versa, an affix which is specifically called a पित् loses its general character of ङित्.
In the Benedictive we have ऊर्णूयात् or ऊर्णुविषीष्ट or ऊर्णविषीष्ट ॥ In the Aorist the 3rd. P. Sing. is और्णोवीत्, dual. और्णुविष्टाम् । The following sûtra gives alternative forms.

entries.english: 2450. Instead of the first five tense-affixes, in the Present tense of the Parasmaipada coming after the verb 'bru' (to speak) there may optionally be the affixes of the Perfect; and 'aha' is at the same time, the substitute in the room of 'bru'. The अ is for the sake of utterance only; the real substitute is आह् ॥ Thus आह ‘he says’; आहतुः ‘they two say’; आहुः ‘they say’; आत्थ ‘thou sayst’; आहथुः ‘you two say’; the rest like ब्रू as shown below:— Singular. Dual. Plural. Third Person. आह or ब्रवीति आहतुः or ब्रूतः आहुः or ब्रुवन्ति Second Person. आत्थ or ब्रवीषि आहथुः or ब्रूथः ब्रूथ First Person. ब्रवीमि ब्रूवः ब्रूमः —:0:— The word आदितः 'first' is used in the sûtra to indicate that the substitution should not take place in the case of the last four affixes. The repetition of the word ब्रुवः in the sûtra indicates the original expression which is to be replaced; and shows that this change occurs in the Parasmaipada affixes only. In forming the second Person singular आह + थ the following sûtra applies.

entries.english: 2451. For the ह of the root आह, there is substituted थ before a jhal letter. Thus आह् + थ = आथ् + थ = आत्थ ॥ As इदमात्थ, किमात्थ. The word आथ् + थ becomes आत्थ by VIII. 4. 55. S. 121. The word झलि is understood here. Hence there is no change before vowel affixes, as आह, आहतुः, आहुः ॥

entries.english:
2452. Before a पित् Sârvadhâtuka affix beginning with a consonant, the augment ईट् is placed after ब्रू ॥

As ब्रवीति, ब्रवीषि, ब्रवीमि, अब्रवीत् ॥ But ब्रवाणि before such an affix beginning with a vowel, and ब्रूवः before an affix which is not पित् ॥

The augment ईट् ought to have come in आत्थ also, because थ being a substitute of the पित् affix for ब्रू will be considered as पित् by the rule of sthânivadbhâva (I. 1. 56. S. 49). But the augment does not come, because the थ substitution for थस् by the last aphorism takes place only before a non-vowel affix for झलि is understood. That rule would have become redundant, if we could make the form आतीथ ॥

In the Section treating of the rules that apply to ârdhadhâtuka affixes, we have the following sûtra, which applies to this root when an ârdhadhâtuka affix follows, such as the affixes of the Perfect.

entries.english:
2453. वच् is the substitute of ब्रू 'to speak' when any ârdhadhâtuka affix is to be applied.

Thus the Perfect of brū is formed from vach; as उवाच । ऊचतुः । ऊचुः 2nd. उवचिथ or उवक्थ 1st. ऊचे । The First Fut. is वक्ता 'he will speak.' The इ of वचि is for the sake of articulation only. The substitute being like the principal, वच् is Âtmanepadî when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent, as ऊचे 'he spoke,' वक्ष्यते 'he will speak.'

In the Imperative one form is ब्रवीतु with the ईट् of S. 2452: but the affix तातङ् VII. 1. 35. S. 2197. which replaces तु is not considered पित्, because of the maxim already mentioned before “a ‹?› is not ‹?›, nor a ‹?› should be considered ‹?› for the purposes of operations depending on them.” Therefore we have ब्रूतात् and not ब्रवीतात् । 1st Sing. ब्रवाणि । A. ब्रवै । Pot. ब्रूयात् । Ben. उच्यात् ।

In the Aorist, the affix अङ् is added by III. 1. 52. S. 2438. When अङ् is added the following applies.

2454. The augment उम् is added after the अ of वच् in the अङ्-Aorist.

As अवोचत्, अवोचेताम्, अवोचन् ॥ See III. 1. 52. S. 2438.

अथ शास्यन्ताः परस्मैपदिनः । इङ् त्वात्मनेपदी ।

The following roots upto शास् are Parasmaipadi. But the root इङ् is Âtmanepadi.

३६ इण् गतौ । एति । इतः ॥

The Present 3rd S. is एति । D. इतः । In forming the plural, the following rule applies.

2455. For the इ of the root इण् (एति) is substituted a semivowel (य्), before an affix beginning with a vowel.

Thus यन्ति, यन्तु, आयन् । This supersedes इयङ् substitution, and is, itself superseded by VII. 2. 115, and VII. 3. 84 which ordain Vṛiddhi and Guṇa: on the maxim मध्येऽपवादाः पूर्वान् विधीन् बाधन्ते नापरान् ॥ “Apavâdas that are surrounded by the rules which teach operations that have to be superseded by the apavâda operations, supersede only those rules that precede, not those that follow them.”

So we have अयनम् and आयकः ॥

The perfect 3rd S. is इयाय । In forming the dual the following sûtra applies.

2456. A long vowel is substituted in the reduplicate of the root इण् (एति), before a Personal ending of the Perfect, which has an indicatory क् ॥

As ईयतुः, ईयुः ॥ These are thus formed इ + अतुस् = य् + अतुस् (य् substituted for इ by VI. 4. 81. S. 2455.) Then there is reduplication, the य् becomes sthânivat to इ by I. 1. 59, S. 2243 and we have इ + यतुस् and then by the present rule ईयतुः ॥

Why do we say before a कित् affix? Observe इयाय, इययिथ ॥

The 2nd S. is इययिथ or इयेथ । The First Fut. is एता । The Imperative 3rd S. is एतु, 2nd S. इहि, 1st S. अयानि । The Imperfect is ऐत्, d. ऐताम्, Pl. आयन् ॥ Pot. इयात् । Ben. ईयात् । But this long ई which was obtained by VII. 4. 25. S. 2298 is shortened after an upasarga by the following.

2457. The short vowel is substituted for the simple (अण्) vowel of the stem (एति) before the augment यासुट् in the Benedictive, when a Preposition precedes it.

As निर्विद्यात् । अभिवियात् । अपियात् । परियात् ॥ This is an exception to VII. 4. 25 S. 2298 by which a long would have been substituted. But ईयात् without a Preposition. The ह्रस्वः (VII. 4. 13. S. 834.) is understood here also. Therefore form of ए will not be shortened, as प्रा + ईयात् = प्रेयात्, समेयात् ॥

But in अभि + ईयात् = अभीयात् — the long ई obtained by ekâdeśa is not shortened, because it is not preceded by an upasarga; for there is no upasarga; and there is no long after अभि, for the analysis of अभीयात् gives us अभि + ईयात् । Nor can you say that the rule of अन्तादिवत् (VI. 1. 85 S. 75) should apply here, and this ekâdeśa long ई should be considered as the beginning of the succeeding form, because the present rule of shortening depends upon the fulfilment of two conditions—1. A preposition to precede, and 2. A long vowel to succeed. They being so mutually inter-dependent, that VI. 1. 85 S. 75 cannot apply.

Why do we say the simple अण् vowels are shortened? Observe उप + ईयात् = उपेयात् । The ए obtained by गुण is not shortened, because it is not an अण् vowel.

The समीयात् is not from this root, but from the Bhvâdi root ईङ् गतौ (no 342. A.) The proper form of the Benedictive from the Adâdi is समियात् ॥

The Aorist is formed by substituting √ गा in the place of √ इण् by the following.

entries.english:
2458. गा is the substitute of the root इण् when लुङ् follows. When गा is substituted, the aorist sign सिच् is elided by II. 4. 77. S. 2223. अगात् 'he went.' अगाताम् 'they two went' अगुः 'they all went.'

Note:—The repetition of the word लुङ् in this sûtra, though its anuvṛitti was current from the last Ashṭâdhyâyî aphorisms, indicates that there is no option allowed even in the Âtmanepada, गा being the invariable substitute in all the Padas. Thus अगायि भवता 'you went.' The form अगात् is thus evolved ‹?› + गा + सिच् ‹?› गात् (II. 4. 77. S. 2223.)

इ ३६ गतौ ।
36. इण् to go.

३७ अध्ययने ।

entries.sutra_ocr: 'गातिस्था - ' (२२२३) इति सिचो लुक् । श्रगात् । श्रगाताम् । चगुः ।

entries.english:
2459. गाङ् is the substitute of इङ् when लिट् (Perfect) follows.

Or rather the substitution takes place in anticipation of the adding of the लिट् affixes. Therefore in reduplication, गाङ् is not considered as sthânivat to इङ्, for if it were so, then the sûtra I. 1. 59. S. 2243 would require ‹?› in the reduplicate.

The Perfect 3rd S. is अधिजगे, dual अधिजगाते, pl. अधिजगिरे । The First Future is अध्येता । The Second Future is अध्येष्यते । The Imperative अध्ययै is formed thus : अधि + इ + ऐ = अधि + ए + ऐ = अधि + य् + ऐ = अध्ययै । The guṇa and ‹?› substitutions take place first, and then the Conjunction takes place with the upasarga, whose इ is then changed to य् । This is in contravention to the general maxim that a root must first combine with the Preposition: for in that view, the rule of सवर्णदीर्घ being antaranga would have applied prior to the application of the guṇa rule: namely अधि + इ + ऐ would have become first अधी + ऐ and then guṇa अधे + ऐ = अधै । But this is not the correct form; and this we infer from Pâṇini himself using the form in the sûtra विभाषाऽधीयने (VII. 2. 26 S. 3066). The form अध्यै is thus evolved अधि + इ + आवै = अधि + इ + आवै = अध्यै । Had the root combined first with the preposition, then this form could not have been got. The employment of the form अध्यै by Pâṇini himself shows that the rule पूर्वे धातुरुपसर्गेण &c. does not apply to अधि + इङ् ।

The Imperfect (लङ्) third person singular is अध्यैत (अधि + आट् + इ + त VI. 4. 72. S. 2254 = अधि + ऐ + त S. 269. अध्यैत) । In forming the dual, the equation stands thus अधि + आट् + इ + आताम् । Here the इयङ् substitution for इ takes place first, because it is taught by VI. 4. 77 S. 271, a rule subsequent in Ashṭâdhyâyî order to the rule ordaining आट्, namely VI. 4. 72 S. 2254. When इ is thus replaced by इयङ् then comes आट् । Then आट् and इ of इयङ् coalesce into Vṛiddhi by S. 269. Thus अधि + आ + इय् + आताम् = अधि + ऐ + आताम् (VI. 1. 90 S. 269) अध्यैयाताम् । The plural is अध्यैयत (अधि + आ + इय् + अत, the अत is replaced by झा VII. 1. 5. S. 2258). The first person Singular is अधि + आ + इ + इ = अधि + ऐय् + इ = अध्यैयि । The dual is अध्यैवहि ।

The Potential 3rd Per. S. is अधीयीत and is thus formed अधि + इ + सीयुट् + त = अधि + इ + ईय् + त, the त is elided by VII. 2. 79 S. 2211 = अधि + इय् + ईय् + त, the इयङ् substitution by VI. 4. 77 S. 271—अधीयीत, the य् is elided by VI. 1. 66. S. 873. The dual is अधीयीयाताम् । The Second person plural is अधीयीध्वम् । The first person Singular is अधीयीय ।

The Benedictive 3rd pers. Singular is अध्येषीष्ट । Thus अधि + इ + सीयुट् + सुट् + त ॥ Here by III. 4. 107 S. 2210 there is सुट् । The dual is अध्येषीयास्ताम्, and the plural is अध्येषीरन् ॥

The Aorist (लुङ्) of अधि + इङ् is optionally formed from another stem, namely from √गाङ् as the following sûtra shows.

2460. In the Aorist and the Conditional Tenses, गाङ् is optionally substituted for the root इङ् ।

Thus अधि + इ + त = अधि + आट् + इ + सिच् + त VI. 4. 72 S. 2254 = अधि + आट् + गा + त + सिच् + त ।

This Substitute should not be confounded with the root √गा । A peculiarity of this substitute is that all affixes except ङित् or णित् after it are considered as ङित् and so cause no guṇa or vṛiddhi &c. This is done by the following sûtra :—

2461. All affixes after गाङ् (the substitute of इङ्) and after the कुटादि roots are treated as if they had an indicatory ङ्, except णिन् or णित् affixes.

Thus अधि + आट् + गा + सिच् + त = अधि + अगा + 0 + त = अध्यगात । Now the following sûtra applies by which गा is changed to गी ।
entries.note: Devanagari sutra line is at the foot of page 285; English heading begins at top of page 286.

entries.english:
2462. For the final of the roots called ghu, as well as of mâ, sthâ, gâ, pâ, hâ, and so, there is substituted ईत् before an ârdhadhâtuka affix beginning with a consonant, which has an indicatory क् or ङ् ।

By the preceding sûtra, affixes after गा are ङित् ; and therefore by the present sûtra गा becomes गी । Thus अधि + आट् + गा + सिच् + त = अध्यगीष्ट ।

But the substitution of गा for इङ् is optional. When there is no substitution, we have अधि + आट् + इ + सिच् + त = अधि + ऐ + स् + त (VI. 1. 90 S. 269) = अध्येष्ठ ।

The Conditional is अध्यगीष्यत or अध्येष्यत ।

entries.english: 38 ✓ik (Parasmaipadi) to remember. This root like the preceding, is also invariably found with the preposition adhi. Because we find Pāṇini himself using the word adhigārtha in sūtra II. 3. 52. S. 613 in the sense of remembering, with the preposition adhi. If this root conveyed the sense of remembering without adhi, then Pāṇini would have used the word igartha इगर्थ in that sūtra, and not adhigartha. Vart:— It should be stated that ✓ik is treated like ✓iṅ: so that there is iyaṅ (S. 2455) substitutions here also. Thus Present Pl. अधियन्ति । The aorist is अध्यगात् । But according to some this rule is confined to ārdhadhātuka affixes only i. e., इक् is like इङ् so far as ārdhadhātuka affixes go; but not to sārvadhātuka affixes. Therefore there is no ‹?› of VI. 4. 81. S. 2455 in their opinion: on the contrary यण् comes. As the present participle अधीयन् used by Bhaṭṭi in the following verse ससीतयोः राघवयोरधीयन् = स्मरन् । (२) । This is the view of Ātreya. According to him the Pre. Pl. is not अधियन्ति, but अधि + इयन्ति or अधीयन्ति ॥ Haradatta is against this view. entries.english: 2463. In the opinion of Śākaṭāyana only, 'jus' is the substitute of 'jhi', in the Imperfect of the roots which end in a long 'Ā'. Thus अयुः । In the alternative, we have अयान् । NOTE:— Why is लङ् repeated here, when the context would have supplied this word; for the sūtra applies to ङित् tenses, of which लुङ् being dealt with in the last, would leave लङ् only to be dealt with by this aphorism, for no other ङित् tense (like लिङ् or लङ्) can end in आ? The repetition shows that the rule applies to those affixes which come after लङ् as लङ्, and not to those which come after another tense which is treated like लङ् । Thus लोट् is treated like लङ्, but for the purposes of this rule, it would not be so treated. Thus the झि of या will not be changed into जुस् by III. 4. 109. Thus बिभ्यतु यातु विदन्तु । The word एव has been used in the sūtra for the sake of the subsequent sūtra. वा ४१ गतिगन्धनयोः । गन्धनं सूचनम् । 41. ✓vā 1. to go. 2. to blow. The word gandhanam here is synonymous with sūcanā. This root is conjugated in the Sārvadhātuka tenses only. It never takes the affixes of the ārdhadhātuka class. Thus it is a defective root, not having all the tenses. It should not be confounded with the substitute √ khyā that replaces chakshin (See Adādi 4.) That khyā, of course, takes ārdhadhātuka affixes.
The reason of our confining this root to Sārvadhātuka affixes is this. If this root were capable of taking ārdhadhātuka affixes, then we could form the noun ‹?› from it by adding the ārdhadhātuka affix ‹?›. But we cannot do so: if we want to get the word ‹?› we must derive it from ‹?› of √ चक्षिङ् (II. 4. 54. S. 2436). For that ‹?› is really ‹?›, the ‹?› is changed to ‹?›, and this ‹?› is considered asiddha. Therefore in नमः ख्यात्रे the visarga is not changed to the jihvāmūlīya ‹?›, by VIII. 3. 37. S. 142; because ‹?› is considered to be followed by ‹?›, a ‹?› letter, and so the visarga retains its form by VIII. 3. 35. S. 150. Had however ‹?› in नमः ख्यात्रे been derived from this ‹?›, then nothing could have prevented the application of VIII. 3. 37. S. 143, and we would have got jihvāmūlīya in नमः ख्यात्रे ।
Under the sutra चक्षिङः ख्याञ् (II. 4. 54. S. 2436) the Mahabhashya reads several vartikas: one of them is Vart:—The substitute is ‹?›; i.e. ‹?›. The reason of this is given in the subsequent vartikas: one of which is ‹?› । Vart:—The substitute is to be considered as khśāñ, in order to prevent samsthāna modification of visarga in namaḥ khyâtre. Samsthāna is the technical term for jihvāmūlīya, in the terminology of ancient grammarians. The necessity of making ‹?› substitute ‹?› is to prevent this jihvāmūlīya change.
We learn from the implication of this vartika and its explanation in the Mahabhashya that the present root never takes ārdhadhātuka affixes.
This root, according to the author of Nyāsa, can never be preceded by the preposition सम् । That is we never find the form ‹?›. The form ‹?› &c., is from the substitute √ ‹?› and not from this root. See III. 2. 7. S. 2921.
According to the Mādhavīya Vritti, this root should also be considered as if it was ‹?›, just like the substitute for the purposes of Ārdhadhātuka affixes. According to Ātreya it is conjugated only in the ārdhadhātuka form, others conjugate it generically, without confining it to ārdhadhātuka affixes.
The word ‹?› is derived from this root. The word ‹?› is changed to ‹?› by Uṇādi IV. 136.
According to the Mādhavīya, this root when taking Ārdhadhātuka affixes, is treated just like ‹?› obtained from ‹?›; and so the noun formed from this root is just like ‹?› derived from root. But Bhattoji does not agree with this opinion. According to the Mādhavīya it would be conjugated in all Moods and Tenses; and not confined to Sārvadhātuka only.

entries.english:
2465. The form विदाङ्कुर्वन्तु is optionally employed as an irregular form in the Imperative.
This irregular form is obtained by adding the affix आम् to the root विद् 'to know', when followed by लोट् or the Imperative tense; the tense affixes of लोट् are then elided by luk; moreover there is no substitution of guṇa as required by VII. 3. 86; and when we have thus obtained the form विदा, we annex to it the लोट् of the verb कृ; thus we have विदाङ्कुर्वन्तु or विदन्तु 'let them know.' The third person plural is not only intended to be spoken of by the employment of the form विदाङ्कुर्वन्तु in the aphorism; on the contrary, the word shows that all the numbers and persons of the Imperative may be so employed; as विदाङ्करोतु, विदाङ्कुरुताम् &c.
In other words the Periphrastic Imperative is formed by adding to विदा the Imperative of the root कृ. To form the Imperative of kṛ, the following sûtras apply; it being remembered that the root √ kṛ belongs to the Tanâdi class.
entries.note: SK number misread in OCR as 2485; fixed to 2465 by strict sequence.

entries.english:
2466. The affix उ comes after the roots of the Tanâdi class and after the verb कृ 'to make' when a sârvadhâtuka affix follows, signifying the agent.
This debars शप्. As सन् + उ + ति = सनोति 'he expands'; कृ + उ + ति = करोति 'he makes'. Though the root कृ is included in the list of the Tanâdi verbs, for which see Dhâtupâṭha, yet its separate enunciation in the present sûtra is for the sake of showing that the operations dependent upon a word being included in a gaṇa or class, are not of universal validity. Therefore forms like विश्वसेत् are valid, as in the sentence, न विश्वसेदविश्वस्तम् । Here there is not the elision of शप् in विश्वस् though the root belongs to the adâdi class (No. 60). According to the Kâśikâ, the separate enunciation of कृ in this sûtra is for the sake of making a restrictive rule with regard to this verb; that is to say, the root कृ is a Tanâdi root only for the purposes of taking the affix उ; all the other operations of Tanâdi verbs are not to be performed upon it. Thus the rule II. 4. 79, does not apply to कृ; the elision is compulsory and not optional.
Thus the 3rd Person Singular is विदाङ्करोतु. In forming the 3rd Per. Singular with तात् or of the Dual, &c. of the Imperative of कृ, the following applies.
entries.note: Embedded Devanagari restored from plain context.

entries.english:
2467. Before a Sârvadhâtuka affix with an indicatory क् or ङ्, short उ is substituted for the अ of (कृ + उ) when gunated.
Note :— Thus कृ + उ + तस् = कर् + उ + तस् (VII. 3. 84) = कु + उ + तस् = कुरुतः (VI. 4. 110). The तस् is ङित् by I. 2. 4. So also कुर्वन्ति, कुरु. Why do we say 'before a Sârvadhâtuka'? So that the rule may apply to what was once a Sârvadhâtuka, though no longer existent. Thus कुरु where the personal ending हि is elided, but it leaves its effect behind.
The त् in उत् shows that this उ is not to be gunated by VII. 3. 86. When the affix is not ङित् or णित्, we have करवाणि, करवाव and करवाम (I. 2. 4).
Thus we have विदाङ्कुरुतात् । D. विदाङ्कुरुताम् ।
In forming the 2nd Person Singular, the हि is elided by VI. 4. 106. S. 2234. This elision of हि is ordained by a sûtra which falls in the subdivision of asiddhas, under असिद्धवदत्राभात् (VI. 4. 22. S. 2183); and therefore, it is considered to have not taken place for the purposes of a change required by VI. 4. 110. S. 2467. Therefore we have the form कुरु though no sârvadhâtuka affix follows. Thus विदाङ्कुरु । 1st Sing. विदाङ्करवाणि ।
The Imperfect 3rd S. is अवेत्; D. अविताम् । The Plural is formed by जुस् under III. 4. 109. S. 2226. Thus अविदुः । In the 2nd Singular, there is substitution of रु by the following :—

2469. Before a Sârvadhâtuka kit or ṅit affix, the a of śna and as is elided.

Śna is the characteristic of the roots of the Rudhâdi class, while as is the root itself. Thus रुन्धः ; इन्धे, भिन्तः, भिन्दन्ति ; So also of अस् :—स्तः, सन्ति । But भिनत्ति and भिन्धि before non-kit and non-ṅit affixes. śna + as ought to be śnâs, instead of that we have śnas in the sûtra. The pararûpa single substitution is an irregularity.

entries.english:
2470. Bhû is the substitute of the verb as 'to be,' when an ârdhadhâtuka affix is to be applied.

Thus बभूव । Fut. भविता 'he will be,' भवितुम् 'in order to be,' भवितव्यम् 'must be.' Note:—Now the Perfect tense affixes are also ârdhadhâtuka affixes (III. 4. 115). The Perfect of अस् is therefore the same as that of भू, namely, बभूव &c. There is, however, an important exception to this rule, namely, when as is employed as an auxiliary verb in forming Periphrastic Perfect of other verbs. In that case अस् forms its Perfect tense regularly, आस, आसतुः, आसुः &c. This apparent breach of the present sûtra is explained by taking the term कास् in III. 1. 40 as a Pratyâhâra including kâs, pratyaya, and as, and if we could not form its Perfect in the regular way, its inclusion in this Pratyâhâra would be useless; hence we conclude, that as an auxiliary verb, as forms its Perfect regularly.

The Imperative is अस्तु or स्तात् । 3rd स्ताम् । Pl. सन्तु । In the Second Person Singular as + hi the following applies:—

2471. For the final vowel of the roots dâ and dhâ (ghu), and for the s of as, edh is substituted before the Imperative ending hi; and thereby the reduplicated syllable of dâ and dhâ is elided.

Thus (dehi, and dhehi, of ghu, and) edhi of as, the as is elided by this sûtra, and a is elided by VI. 4. 111. S. 2469. This edh of the present sûtra should be considered as having an indicatory ś so that the whole of the reduplicate and not only the final letter of the abhyâsa (I. 1. 55) is elided.

Sing. Dual. Plural.
अस्तु स्ताम् सन्तु
एधि स्तम् स्त
असानि असाव असाम
आसीत् आस्ताम् आसन्
आसीः आस्तम् आस्त
आसम् आस्व आस्म

This edh ordained by the present sûtra is considered asiddha, as it falls in the âbhîya section (VI. 4. 22. S. 2183) and therefore hi is changed to dhi by VI. 4. 101, S. 2425, for it is considered to have come after a jhal letter s, though this no longer exists. But when tâtâṅ is added in the Imperative Second Singular, there is no change of the sa of as. Because the tâtâṅ is ordained by a subsequent sûtra, and debars it. Even after the adding of tâtâṅ, there is no change by considering it as sthânivat to its principal hi, on the maxim that a 'rule once set aside, is set aside for good.'

Thus we have स्तात् । स्तम् । स्त । असानि । असाव । असाम । In the Imperfect we have îṭ by VII. 3. 96. S. 2225 as आसीत् । In the dual, there is âṭ augment before स्ताम् (VI. 4. 72. S. 2254), because the elision of a by S. 2469 is asiddha, it being an âbhîya rule, and hence स्ताम् is considered as beginning with vowel. Thus we have आस्ताम् । Pl. आसन् । Pot. स्यात् । Ben. भूयात् । Aor. अभूत् । This is thus derived, a + bhû + cli + t = a + bhû + 0 + t (the sic is elided by II. 4. 77. S. 2223). Now the apṛkta îṭ required by VII. 3. 96. S. 2225 is not added, as we have already explained under that sûtra, that îṭ comes only then when sip and tip exist as si and ti. See page 31 of this volume. Therefore we have अभूत् ।

The sa of as is changed to ṣa when preceded by an alterant preposition by the following :—

entries.english:
2472. The sa of the verb as is changed to ṣa when it is followed by a vowel or ya and is preceded by prâdur, or an upasarga having i or u in it.

The word yaci paraḥ means 'followed by ya or ac'. The word prâduḥ is an Indeclinable, meaning 'evidently.'

Thus अभिष्यन्ति, निष्यन्ति, विष्यन्ति, प्रादुःष्यन्ति, अभिष्यात्, निष्यात्, विष्यात्, प्रादुःष्यात् ॥

Why do we say "when it is followed by a vowel or ya"? Observe अभिस्तः, विस्तः, दुस्तः ॥

2473. The Vṛiddhi (आर्) is substituted for the root vowel (ऋ) of the stem मृज् before any affix that is ordained after a root, provided it is not kit or ṅit ;

As मार्ष्टा, मार्ष्टुम्, मार्ष्टव्यम् । The मृज् here is a root, and the affixes before which this Vriddhi takes place are those which come after roots, and not which come after Pratipadikas. This रुद् + ति । Now applies the following sûtra by which इट् is added even in Sârvadhâtuka affixes:—

entries.english:
2474. A sârvadhâtuka affix beginning with a consonant other than a य्, gets the augment इट् after the root रुद्, and the four that follow it namely, स्वप्, श्वस्, अन and जक्ष् ।

Thus रोदिति, स्वपिति, श्वसिति, प्राणिति, जक्षिति । But जागर्ति which is beyond the five, and रुद्यात् before ârdhadhâtuka affixes, and रुदन्ति before a vowel beginning affix.

The dual is रुदितः । The हि is not changed to धि by VI. 4. 101. S. 2425 by the परत्वात् paribhâshâ, as the इट् augment is subsequently taught. Or in the sûtra VI. 4. 101. S. 2425 we may read the anuvritti of हलि, and it is only when हि begins with a हल् that the rule will apply. Here by the addition of the augment इट्, the affix becomes ajâdi; and so that rule has no scope. Thus रुदिहि ।

In the Imperfect there are ईट् and अद् augments by the following two sûtras.
entries.note: Restored corrupted Devanagari and grammatical terms from plain English context.

entries.english: 2475. After रुद् and the four roots that follow it, comes the augment ईट् to a sârvadhâtuka affix consisting of a single consonant.

2476. According to the opinion of Gârgya, and Gâlava, the augment अद् comes before a Sârvadhâtuka affix consisting of a single consonant, after the above five roots रुद् &c.

Thus we have अरोदीत् with ईट्, or अरोदत् with अद् added to त् । Similarly अरोदीः or अरोदः ।

Note:—As अरोदीत् अरोदीः, अस्वपीत् and अस्वपीः, अश्वसीत्, अश्वसीः, अप्राणीत्, अप्राणीः, अजक्षीत्, अजक्षीः । Why of these five only? Observe अजागर् भवान् ॥ Why an aprikta affix? Observe रोदिति ॥ The word पञ्चभ्यः in the preceding sûtra is singular, though it ought to have been plural.

Note:—As अरोदत् अरोदः, अस्वपत् अस्वपः, अश्वसत् अश्वसः, अप्राणत् अप्राणः, अजक्षत् अजक्षः । The names of Gârgya and Gâlava are mentioned for honoris causa.

Note:—The mention of these names is not for the sake of "option" (विकल्पार्थम्). Because the very injunction about अद्, would make the ईट् of the preceding sûtra optional. The mention of more than one Âchârya in the sûtra is also for this very reason.

In the Potential, the यासुट् augment is added first to the affix, because it is antaranga, as it depends merely on the Mood लिङ्, while with regard to it, the ईट् and अद् augments are Bahiranga, because they depend on a particular base (prakriti such as √rud &c.) and a particular affix (pratyaya, namely only those which are aprikta). Therefore ईट् and अद् augments, though taught subsequent to यासुट् augment, do not debar it, because they are of weaker force compared with it. Therefore यासुट् is added first, and the 3rd Per. S. affix becomes यात्, which being no longer aprikta, there is no occasion for adding to it the augments ईट् or अद् of these two sûtras. Thus we have रुद्यात् ॥

entries.english:
2477. The स् of स्वप् when it assumes the form सुप्, and of सूति, and स्म is changed to ष after सु, वि, निर् and दुर् ॥

The maxim is that the root is first joined with the upasarga, and then grammatical rules applied. Thus the compound verbs are सुस्वप्, विस्वप् &c. To this when the affixes of the Perfect which are कित् are added, then first there is vocalisation of व into उ, and स changed to ष, and then reduplication. That is the steps are (1) सुसुप् (2) सुषुप्, (3) सुषुप् सुप् ।

For the purposes of reduplication the change of स to ष by the rule of Tripâdî ought to have been considered asiddha by VIII. 2. 1. This is prevented by the maxim already given under S. VI. 1. 3. i.e., for the purposes of reduplication, the Tripâdî rules are not asiddha. Therefore ष is reduplicated. Thus we have the following equation सु + स्वप् + अतुस् = सु + सुप + अतुस् (VI. 1. 15. S. 2409) = सु + षुप + अतुस् (VIII. 3. 88. 2477) = सुषुप षुप अतुस् (पूर्वत्रासिद्धीयमद्विर्वचने) = सुषुषुपतुः । So also सुषुषुपुः ।

Before those affixes of लिट् which are not कित्, there is reduplication first, and then vocalisation of the abhyâsa. The change ordained by the present Tripâdî sûtra being considered asiddha (VIII. 2. 1.); the हलादिः शेषः (S. 2179) rule
